zh: 磔迦國，周萬餘里，東據毘播奢河，西臨信度河。國大都城周二十餘里。宜粳稻，多宿麥，出金、銀、鍮石、銅、鐵。時候暑熱，土多風飆。風俗暴惡，言辭鄙褻。衣服鮮白，所謂憍奢耶衣、朝霞衣等。少信佛法，多事天神。伽藍十所，天祠數百。此國已往，多有福舍，以贍貧匱，或施藥，或施食，口腹之資，行旅無累。
en_current: The country of Ṭakka (磔迦國) is over ten thousand *li* in circuit; it borders the Vipāśā River to the east and faces the Sindhu River to the west. The capital city of the country is over twenty *li* in circuit. The land is suitable for non-glutinous rice and produces much winter wheat; it yields gold, silver, brass, copper, and iron. The climate is hot, and the land is subject to many windstorms. The customs of the people are violent and wicked, and their speech is vulgar and obscene. Their clothing is bright white, consisting of so-called *kauśeya* (silk) garments, *chaoxia* (morning glow) robes, and the like. They have little faith in the Buddhadharma and mostly serve the heavenly deities. There are ten *saṃghārāma*s and several hundred *deva* temples. From this country onward, there are many charitable houses (福舍) to provide for the poor and needy, where medicine or food is distributed; with such provisions for their sustenance, travelers are never in want.

zh: 大城西南十四五里，至奢羯羅故城。垣堵雖壞，基趾尚固。周二十餘里。其中更築小城，周六七里，居人富饒；即此國之故都也。數百年前，有王號摩醯邏矩羅（唐言大族），都治此城，王諸印度。有才智，性勇烈，隣境諸國，莫不臣伏。機務餘閑，欲習佛法，令於僧中推一俊德。時諸僧徒莫敢應命，少欲無為，不求聞達；博學高明，有懼威嚴。是時王家舊僮，染衣已久，辭論清雅，言談贍敏，眾共推舉，而以應命。王曰：「我敬佛法，遠訪名僧，眾推此隸，與我談論。常謂僧中，賢明肩比，以今知之，夫何敬哉？」於是宣令五印度國，繼是佛法並皆毀滅，僧徒斥逐無復孑遺。摩揭陀國婆羅阿迭多王（唐曰幼日），崇敬佛法，愛育黎元，以大族王淫刑虐政，自守疆埸，不恭職貢。時大族王治兵將討。幼日王知其聲問，告諸臣曰：「今聞寇至，不忍鬪其兵也。幸諸僚庶赦而不罪，賜此微軀潛行草澤。」言畢出宮，依緣山野。國中感恩慕從者數萬餘人，棲竄海島。大族王以兵付弟，浮海往伐。幼日王守其阨險，輕騎誘戰，金鼓一震，奇兵四起，生擒大族，反接引現。大族王自愧失道，以衣蒙面。幼日王踞師子床，群官周衛，乃命侍臣告大族曰：「汝露其面，吾欲有辭。」大族對曰：「臣主易位，怨敵相視，既非交好，何用面談？」再三告示，終不從命。於是宣令數其罪曰：「三寶福田，四生攸賴。苟任豺狼，傾毀勝業。福不祐汝，見擒於我。罪無可赦，宜從刑辟。」時幼日王母博聞強識，善達占相。聞殺大族也，疾告幼日王曰：「我甞聞大族奇姿多智，欲一見之。」幼日王命引大族至母宮中。幼日母曰：「嗚呼，大族幸勿恥也！世間無常，榮辱更事，吾猶汝母，汝若吾子，宜去蒙衣，一言面對。」大族曰：「昔為敵國之君，今為俘囚之虜，隳廢王業，亡滅宗祀，上愧先靈，下慚黎庶，誠恥面目。俯仰天地，不勝自喪，故此蒙衣。」王母曰：「興廢隨時，存亡有運。以心齊物，則得喪俱忘；以物齊心，則毀譽更起。宜信業報，與時推移，去蒙對語，或存軀命。」大族謝曰：「苟以不才，嗣膺王業，刑政失道，國祚亡滅，雖在縲紲之中，尚貪旦夕之命。敢承大造，面謝厚恩。」於是去蒙衣，出其面。王母曰：「子其自愛，當終爾壽。」已而告幼日王曰：「先典有訓，宥過好生。今大族王積惡雖久，餘福未盡，若殺此人，十二年中，菜色相視。然有中興之氣，終非大國之王，當據北方，有小國土。」幼日王承慈母之命，愍失國之君，娉以稚女，待以殊禮，總其遺兵，更加衛從，未出海島。大族王弟還國自立，大族失位，藏竄山野，北投迦濕彌羅國。迦濕彌羅王深加禮命，愍以失國，封以土邑。歲月既淹，率其邑人，矯殺迦濕彌羅王而自尊立。乘其戰勝之威，西討健馱邏國，潛兵伏甲，遂殺其王，國族大臣，誅鋤殄滅。毀窣堵波，廢僧伽藍，凡一千六百所。兵殺之外，餘有九億人，皆欲誅戮，無遺噍類。時諸輔佐咸進諫曰：「大王威懾強敵，兵不交鋒，誅其首惡。黎庶何咎？願以微躬，代所應死。」王曰：「汝信佛法，崇重冥福，擬成佛果，廣說本生，欲傳我惡於未來世乎？汝宜復位，勿有再辭。」於是以三億上族，臨信度河流殺之；三億中族，下沈信度河流殺之；三億下族，分賜兵士，於是持其亡國之貨，振旅而歸。曾未改歲，尋即徂落。于時，雲霧冥晦，大地震動，暴風奮發。時證果人愍而歎曰：「枉殺無辜，毀滅佛法，墮無間獄，流轉未已。」奢羯羅故城中有一伽藍，僧徒百餘人，並學小乘法。世親菩薩昔於此中製《勝義諦論》。其側窣堵波，高二百餘尺，過去四佛於此說法。又有四佛經行遺迹之所。伽藍西北五六里，有窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也，是過去四佛說法之處。新都城東北十餘里，至石窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也，是如來往北方行化中路止處。《印度記》曰：「窣堵波中有多舍利，或有齋日，時放光明。」
en_current: Fourteen or fifteen *li* to the southwest of the great city, one reaches the old city of Śākala (奢羯羅故城). Although the walls are ruined, the foundations remain solid. It is over twenty *li* in circumference. Within it, a smaller city has been built, six or seven *li* in circumference, where the inhabitants are wealthy; this is the former capital of this country. Several hundred years ago, there was a king named Mihirakula (摩醯邏矩羅) (translated as "Great Clan" in Chinese), who made this city his capital and ruled over all of India. He possessed talent and wisdom, and his nature was brave and fierce; there was no neighboring country that did not submit to him. During his leisure from state affairs, he wished to study the Buddha-dharma and ordered the monks to recommend a person of outstanding virtue. At that time, the monks dared not respond to the order, for they were few in desire and practiced non-action, not seeking fame or status; those who were learned and brilliant feared his majesty. At that time, there was a former servant of the royal household who had long worn the dyed robes (i.e., was a monk), whose rhetoric was refined and elegant, and whose speech was eloquent and quick; the assembly collectively recommended him to respond to the order. The King said, "I respect the Buddha-dharma and have sought out famous monks from afar, yet the assembly recommends this menial to engage in discussion with me. I always thought that among the monks, the wise and brilliant were comparable; now that I know this, what is there to respect?" Thereupon, he issued a decree throughout the five regions of India that from then on, the Buddha-dharma was to be utterly destroyed, and all monks were to be expelled until not a single one remained. King Bālāditya (婆羅阿迭多) (translated as "Young Sun" in Chinese) of the country of Magadha (摩揭陀國) revered the Buddha-dharma and loved his people; because of King Mihirakula’s excessive punishments and tyrannical rule, he guarded his own borders and did not offer the customary tribute. At that time, King Mihirakula mobilized his troops, intending to punish him. When King Bālāditya (幼日王) learned of this news, he told his ministers, "I hear the invaders are coming, but I cannot bear to let my soldiers engage in battle. I hope my officials and the common people will forgive me for this, and I shall take this humble body and hide in the marshes and wilderness." Having finished speaking, he left the palace and took refuge in the mountains and forests. Several tens of thousands of people in the country, moved by gratitude and admiration, followed him and hid on islands in the sea. King Mihirakula (大族王) entrusted his troops to his younger brother and sailed across the sea to attack him. King Bālāditya guarded the strategic passes and sent light cavalry to lure the enemy into battle; at the first sound of the gongs and drums, ambushers rose from all sides, capturing Mihirakula alive and leading him forward with his hands tied behind his back. King Mihirakula, ashamed of his failure, covered his face with his garment. King Bālāditya sat upon his lion throne, surrounded by his officials, and ordered his attendants to say to Mihirakula, "Uncover your face, for I have words for you." Mihirakula replied, "The positions of subject and master have been reversed, and we look upon each other as enemies; since we are not on friendly terms, what is the use of speaking face to face?" Though they urged him again and again, he would not comply. Thereupon, the King issued a proclamation enumerating his crimes, saying, "The Three Jewels are a field of merit upon which the four forms of birth depend. You have acted like a jackal or wolf, destroying these noble works. Fortune has not protected you, and you have been captured by me. Your crimes are unpardonable, and you must face the penalty of the law." At that time, the mother of King Bālāditya was widely learned and possessed a keen memory, and she was highly skilled in physiognomy. Hearing that he was about to execute Mihirakula, she hurriedly told King Bālāditya, "I have heard that Mihirakula possesses an extraordinary appearance and great wisdom; I wish to see him once." King Bālāditya ordered that Mihirakula be led into his mother's palace. The mother of Bālāditya (幼日王) said, "Alas, Mihirakula (大族), I pray you do not feel ashamed! The world is impermanent, and honor and disgrace alternate. I am like a mother to you, and you are like a son to me; you should remove the cloth covering your face and speak to me face to face."  Mihirakula said, "Formerly the ruler of a hostile state, I am now a captive prisoner. Having ruined the royal enterprise and extinguished the ancestral sacrifices, I am ashamed before the spirits of my ancestors above and the common people below; I am truly disgraced to show my face. Looking up and down between heaven and earth, I cannot bear the loss of myself, and that is why I cover my face."  The king's mother said, "Rise and fall follow the times; existence and extinction have their destiny. If you use the mind to equalize things, then gain and loss are both forgotten; if you use things to equalize the mind, then praise and blame arise in turn. You should believe in karmic retribution and move along with the times. Remove your covering and speak; perhaps you may preserve your life."  Mihirakula thanked her, saying, "Being a man of no talent, I inherited the royal throne, yet my governance strayed from the Way, leading to the ruin of my kingdom. Although I am now in bonds, I still cling to the hope of living for a little longer. I dare to accept your great kindness and will uncover my face to thank you for your profound grace."  Thereupon, he removed the cloth and revealed his face. The king's mother said, "Take care of yourself, for you shall live out your natural lifespan."  Soon after, she told King Bālāditya, "The ancient scriptures contain the teaching to forgive transgressions and cherish life. Although King Mihirakula has accumulated evil for a long time, his remaining merit is not yet exhausted. If you kill this man, for twelve years there will be famine and suffering. However, he possesses the energy of a restoration; he will not ultimately be a king of a great country, but he shall occupy the north and possess a small territory." King Bālāditya, obeying his compassionate mother's command and pitying the sovereign who had lost his kingdom, gave him a young daughter in marriage and treated him with extraordinary courtesy; he assembled the king's remaining troops and provided additional guards before they had even left the island. The younger brother of King Mihirakula returned to his country and established himself as ruler; having lost his throne, Mihirakula fled to hide in the mountains and wilderness, eventually seeking refuge in the north in the kingdom of Kaśmīra (迦濕彌羅國). The King of Kaśmīra treated him with great courtesy and, pitying him for the loss of his kingdom, granted him a territory as a fief. After some time had passed, he led his townspeople, treacherously killed the King of Kaśmīra, and established himself as ruler. Taking advantage of the prestige of his victory, he attacked the kingdom of Gandhāra (健馱邏國) to the west; by deploying hidden troops and an ambush, he killed its king and completely exterminated the royal clan and the high ministers. He destroyed one thousand six hundred stūpas and sanghārāmas. Beyond those killed in battle, there were nine hundred million people whom he intended to execute, leaving no survivors. At that time, his assistants all remonstrated, saying, "The Great King has intimidated powerful enemies and, without engaging in battle, has executed the chief culprits. What fault have the common people committed? We wish to offer our own humble bodies to die in their stead." The King replied, "You believe in the Buddha-dharma, value merit in the afterlife, aspire to attain the fruit of Buddhahood, and speak extensively on the Jātakas; do you wish to transmit my evil deeds to future generations? You should return to your positions and speak no more of this." Thereupon, he took three hundred million of the upper-class families and had them killed at the bank of the Sindhu (信度) River; three hundred million of the middle-class families were drowned and killed in the Sindhu River; and three hundred million of the lower-class families were distributed among the soldiers. Having seized the wealth of the ruined state, he gathered his troops and returned. Before a year had passed, he suddenly died. At that time, clouds and fog grew dark and gloomy, the great earth shook, and violent winds raged. A person who had attained the fruit (of the path) felt pity and sighed, saying, "By unjustly killing the innocent and destroying the Buddha-dharma, he has fallen into the Avīci hell, to transmigrate without end."  In the old city of Śākala (奢羯羅故城), there is a monastery (saṃghārāma) with more than one hundred monks, all of whom study the Hīnayāna teachings. The Bodhisattva Vasubandhu (世親) formerly composed the *Paramārthasaptati* (勝義諦論) here. Beside it is a stūpa over two hundred feet high, where the four past Buddhas preached the Dharma. There is also a site with traces of the four Buddhas walking in meditation. Five or six li to the northwest of the monastery is a stūpa over two hundred feet high, built by King Aśoka (無憂王), which is the place where the four past Buddhas preached the Dharma. More than ten li to the northeast of the new capital city, one reaches a stone stūpa over two hundred feet high, built by King Aśoka, which is the place where the Tathāgata halted midway while traveling north to spread his teachings. The *Account of India* (印度記) says, "There are many relics within the stūpa, and on days of fasting, it sometimes emits light."

zh: 國大都城周二十餘里。
en_current: The capital city of the kingdom is more than twenty li in circuit.

name_zh: 奢羯羅伽藍西北窣堵波
zh: 伽藍西北五六里，有窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也，是過去四佛說法之處。
en_current: Five or six li to the northwest of the monastery (saṃghārāma 伽藍), there is a stupa (stūpa 窣堵波) over two hundred feet high, built by King Aśoka (無憂王), which is the place where the four buddhas of the past preached the Dharma.

zh: 新都城東北十餘里，至石窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也，是如來往北方行化中路止處。《印度記》曰：「窣堵波中有多舍利，或有齋日，時放光明。」
en_current: More than ten li to the northeast of the new capital city, one reaches a stone stūpa over two hundred feet high, which was built by King Aśoka (無憂王) at the place where the Tathāgata (如來) halted while traveling north to spread his teachings. The *Records of India* (印度記) states: "There are many relics inside the stūpa, which occasionally emit light on fast days."

zh: 從此東行五百餘里，至那僕底國（北印度境）。至那僕底國，周二千餘里。國大都城周十四五里。稼穡滋茂，菓木稀疎。編戶安業，國用豐贍。氣序溫暑，風俗怯弱，學綜真俗，信兼邪正。伽藍十所，天祠八所。昔迦膩色迦王之御宇也，聲振隣國，威被殊俗，河西蕃維，畏威送質。迦膩色迦王既得質子，賞遇隆厚，三時易館，四兵警衛。此國則冬所居也，故曰至那僕底（唐言漢封）。質子所居，因為國號。此境已往，洎諸印度，土無梨、桃，質子所植，因謂桃曰至那爾（唐言漢持來），梨曰至那羅闍弗呾邏（唐言漢王子）。故此國人深敬東土，更相指語：「是我先王本國人也。」
en_current: Traveling eastward from here for more than five hundred li, one arrives at the country of Cīnabhukti (至那僕底國) (within the borders of North India). The country of Cīnabhukti is more than two thousand li in circuit. The capital city is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit. The crops are lush and abundant, but fruit trees are sparse. The households are settled in their occupations, and the national resources are plentiful. The climate is warm and hot; the customs of the people are timid and weak. Their studies encompass both the true and the conventional, and their faith includes both the heterodox and the orthodox. There are ten saṃghārāmas and eight deva temples.  In the past, during the reign of King Kaniṣka (迦膩色迦王), his reputation shook neighboring countries and his might extended to distant lands; the border tribes west of the river feared his power and sent hostages. Once King Kaniṣka had obtained the hostages, he treated them with great generosity and favor, changing their residences according to the three seasons and providing guards from the four branches of the military. This country was his winter residence, and therefore it is called Cīnabhukti (which in the language of the Tang means "Han Fief"). Because it was the place where the hostages resided, it became the name of the country.  From this region onward, as far as the various parts of India, the land had no pears or peaches. They were planted by the hostages, and thus peaches are called *cīnānī* (至那爾) (which in the language of the Tang means "brought from Han"), and pears are called *cīnarājaputra* (至那羅闍弗呾邏) (which in the language of the Tang means "Han Prince"). Therefore, the people of this country deeply revere the eastern lands, and they point to one another and say, "These are the people from the original country of our former king."

zh: 大城東南行五百餘里，至答秣蘇伐那僧伽藍（唐言闍林）。僧徒三百餘人，學說一切有部，眾儀肅穆，德行清高，小乘之學特為博究，賢劫千佛皆於此地集天、人眾，說深妙法。釋迦如來涅槃之後第三百年中，有迦多衍那（舊曰迦旃延，訛也）論師者，於此製《發智論》焉。闍林伽藍中有窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也。其側則有過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之處。小窣堵波、諸大石室，鱗次相望，不詳其數，並是劫初已來諸果聖人，於此寂滅，羌難備舉，齒骨猶在。繞山伽藍周二十里，佛舍利窣堵波數百千所，連隅接影。
en_current: Traveling more than five hundred *li* to the southeast of the great city, one arrives at the Tamasavana Monastery (答秣蘇伐那僧伽藍) (in the Tang language, "Dark Forest"). There are more than three hundred monks who study the Sarvāstivāda school; their deportment is solemn and their moral conduct is lofty, and they are particularly well-versed in the studies of the Lesser Vehicle. The thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa all gathered assemblies of gods and humans in this place to preach the profound and wonderful Dharma. In the three-hundredth year after the Nirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the master Kātyāyana (formerly called Jiazhanyan [迦旃延], which is erroneous) composed the *Jñānaprasthāna-śāstra* here. Within the Tamasavana Monastery, there is a stūpa over two hundred feet high, which was built by King Aśoka. Beside it are the sites of the seats and walking paths of the four past Buddhas. Small stūpas and various large stone chambers stand facing one another like the scales of a fish, in numbers too many to detail; these are all places where the various sages who have attained fruition since the beginning of the *kalpa* have entered into extinction, and it is difficult to enumerate them all, though their teeth and bones still remain. The monasteries surrounding the mountain cover a circuit of twenty *li*, and there are hundreds of thousands of stūpas containing the Buddha’s relics, with their corners connected and their shadows touching.

zh: 從此東北行百四五十里，至闍爛達羅國（北印度境）。闍爛達邏國，東西千餘里，南北八百餘里。國大都城周十二三里。宜穀稼，多粳稻，林樹扶疎，華菓茂盛。氣序溫暑，風俗剛烈，容貌鄙陋，家室富饒。伽藍五十餘所，僧徒二千餘人，大小二乘，專門習學。天祠三所，外道五百餘人，並塗灰之侶也。此國先王崇敬外道，其後遇羅漢，聞法信悟。故中印度王體其淳信，五印度國三寶之事，一以總監。混彼此，忘愛惡，督察僧徒，妙窮淑慝。故道德著聞者，竭誠敬仰；戒行虧犯者，深加責罰。聖迹之所，並皆旌建，或窣堵波，或僧伽藍，印度境內，無不周遍。
en_current: From here, traveling northeast for one hundred forty or fifty li, one arrives at the country of Jālaṃdhara (闍爛達羅國) (in the territory of North India). The country of Jālaṃdhara is over one thousand li from east to west and over eight hundred li from north to south. The capital city of the country is twelve or thirteen li in circumference. It is suitable for grain crops, with an abundance of non-glutinous rice; the forests and trees are lush and spreading, and flowers and fruits are abundant. The climate is warm and hot; the customs of the people are fierce and unyielding, their appearance is coarse and ugly, and their households are wealthy and prosperous. There are more than fifty saṃghārāmas and over two thousand monks, who study both the Great and Lesser Vehicles. There are three Deva temples, and more than five hundred followers of non-Buddhist paths, all of whom are of the sect that smears themselves with ash.  A former king of this country revered non-Buddhist paths, but later he met an arhat, heard the Dharma, and attained faith and enlightenment. Therefore, the king of Mid-India, recognizing his pure faith, entrusted to him the sole supervision of the affairs of the Three Jewels throughout the five Indias. He made no distinction between this and that, forgot preferences and aversions, supervised the monks, and thoroughly discerned the virtuous and the wicked. Thus, those whose moral character was renowned were honored with utmost sincerity, while those who violated the precepts were severely punished. At all sites of sacred traces, he erected memorials, whether stūpas or saṃghārāmas, and there is no place within the territory of India where these are not found.

zh: 從此東北，踰峻嶺越，洞谷，經危途，涉險路，行七百餘里，至屈（居勿反）露多國（北印度境）。屈露多國，周三千餘里，山周四境。國大都城周十四五里。土地沃壤，穀稼時播，華果茂盛，卉木滋榮。既隣雪山，遂多珍藥，出金、銀、赤銅及火珠、雨石。氣序逾寒，霜雪微降。人貌麁弊，既癭且尰，性剛猛，尚氣勇。伽藍二十餘所，僧徒千餘人，多學大乘，少習諸部。天祠十五，異道雜居。依巖據嶺，石室相距，或羅漢所居，或仙人所止。國中有窣堵波，無憂王之建也。在昔如來曾至此國。說法度人，遺迹斯記。
en_current: From here, traveling northeast, crossing steep ridges, traversing deep valleys, passing over perilous routes, and wading through dangerous paths for more than seven hundred *li*, one reaches the country of Kulūta (屈露多國) (屈 is read 居勿反) (within the borders of North India). The country of Kulūta is more than three thousand *li* in circuit, with mountains surrounding its four borders. The capital city of the country is fourteen or fifteen *li* in circuit. The land is fertile, grain is sown in its season, flowers and fruits are abundant, and plants and trees flourish. As it borders the Snow Mountains (Himālaya), it is rich in precious medicinal herbs and produces gold, silver, red copper, as well as fire-pearls and rain-stones. The climate is extremely cold, and frost and snow fall lightly. The people are coarse and ugly in appearance, and are prone to goiters and swollen feet; their nature is fierce and impetuous, and they value spirit and courage. There are more than twenty *saṃghārāmas* (伽藍) with over one thousand monks, most of whom study the Great Vehicle (Mahāyāna), while few practice the various schools (Hīnayāna). There are fifteen *deva* temples, where followers of different paths live together. Relying on cliffs and occupying ridges, stone chambers are situated at intervals, some being dwellings of *arhats* and others being places where *ṛṣis* (仙人) have stayed. In the country there is a *stūpa* built by King Aśoka (無憂王). In the past, the Tathāgata came to this country, preached the Dharma to save people, and this record remains of his traces.

zh: 從此北路千八九百里，道路危險，踰山越谷，至洛護羅國。
en_current: From here, the northern route extends for one thousand eight or nine hundred li; the path is perilous, crossing mountains and traversing valleys, until one reaches the country of Lāhula (洛護羅國).

zh: 此北二千餘里，經途艱阻，寒風飛雪，至秣邏娑國（亦謂三波訶國）。
en_current: More than two thousand li to the north of this place, the route is difficult and obstructed, with cold winds and flying snow, until one reaches the country of Marasā (秣邏娑國) (also called the country of Sampaha (三波訶國)).

zh: 自屈露多國南行七百餘里，越大山，濟大河，至設多圖盧國（北印度境）。設多圖盧國，周二千餘里，西臨大河。國大都城周十七八里。穀稼殷盛，果實繁茂，多金、銀，出珠珍。服用鮮素，裳衣綺靡。氣序暑熱，風俗淳和，人性善順，上下有序。敦信佛法，誠心質敬。王城內外，伽藍十所，庭宇荒涼，僧徒尠少。城東南三四里，有窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也。傍有過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。
en_current: Traveling south from the country of Kulūta (屈露多國) for over seven hundred li, crossing a great mountain and fording a large river, one arrives at the country of Śatadru (設多圖盧國) (within the borders of North India). The country of Śatadru is over two thousand li in circuit and borders a large river to the west. The capital city of the country is seventeen or eighteen li in circuit. The grain crops are abundant, fruits and produce are plentiful, and there is much gold, silver, and precious pearls. The people’s clothing is fresh and plain, though their garments are elegant and fine. The climate is hot, the customs are honest and harmonious, the people are naturally kind and compliant, and there is order between those of high and low status. They are devoted to the Buddha-Dharma and are sincere and respectful in their faith. Inside and outside the royal city, there are ten saṃghārāmas, but the courtyards and buildings are desolate, and the number of monks is small. Three or four li to the southeast of the city, there is a stūpa over two hundred feet high, which was built by King Aśoka. Beside it are the sites of the seats and walking paths of the four past Buddhas.

zh: 復從此西南行八百餘里，至波理夜呾羅國（中印度境）。波理夜呾羅國，周三千餘里。國大都城周十四五里。宜穀稼，豐宿麥，有異稻種六十日而收穫焉。多牛羊，少華菓。氣序暑熱，風俗剛猛。不尚學藝，信奉外道。王，吠奢種也，性勇烈，多武略。伽藍八所，傾毀已甚，僧徒寡少，習學小乘。天祠十餘所，異道千餘人。
en_current: From here, traveling southwest for more than eight hundred li, one arrives at the country of Pāriyātra (波理夜呾羅國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Pāriyātra is more than three thousand li in circuit. The capital city is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit. The land is suitable for grain crops and is abundant in winter wheat; there is a unique variety of rice that is harvested in sixty days. There are many cattle and sheep, but few flowers or fruits. The climate is hot, and the customs of the people are fierce and impetuous. They do not value learning or the arts, and they believe in and practice non-Buddhist paths. The king is of the Vaiśya (吠奢) caste; his nature is brave and fierce, and he possesses much martial strategy. There are eight sanghārāmas, which are in a state of great ruin, and the number of monks is small; they study the Hīnayāna. There are more than ten deva temples, and over one thousand followers of non-Buddhist paths.

zh: 從此東行五百餘里，至秣菟羅國（中印度境）。秣菟羅國，周五千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里，土地膏腴，稼穡是務。菴沒羅菓家植成林，雖同一名，而有兩種：小者生青熟黃，大者始終青色。出細班㲲及黃金。氣序暑熱，風俗善順，好修冥福，崇德尚學。伽藍二十餘所，僧徒二千餘人，大小二乘，兼功習學。天祠五所，異道雜居。有三窣堵波，並無憂王所建也。過去四佛遺迹甚多。釋迦如來諸聖弟子遺身窣堵波，謂舍利子（舊曰舍利子，又曰舍利弗，訛略也）、沒特伽羅子（舊曰目乾連，訛也）、布剌拏梅呾麗衍尼弗呾羅、（唐言滿慈子。舊曰彌多羅尼子，訛略也）、鄔波釐、阿難陀、羅怙羅（舊曰羅睺，又曰羅云，皆訛略也），曼殊室利（唐言妙吉祥。舊曰濡首，又曰文殊師利，或言曼殊尸利，譯曰妙德，訛也）諸菩薩窣堵波等。每歲三長及月六齋，僧徒相競，率其同好，齎持供具，多營奇玩，隨其所宗，而致像設。阿毘達磨眾供養舍利子；習定之徒供養沒特伽羅子；誦持經者供養滿慈子；學毘柰耶眾供養鄔波釐；諸苾芻尼供養阿難；未受具戒者供養羅怙羅；其學大乘者供養諸菩薩。是日也，諸窣堵波競修供養，珠幡布列，寶蓋駢羅，香煙若雲，華散如雨，蔽虧日月，震蕩谿谷。國王大臣，修善為務。
en_current: From here, traveling east more than five hundred *li*, one arrives at the country of Mathurā (秣菟羅國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Mathurā is more than five thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than twenty *li* in circuit. The land is fertile and rich, and the people are devoted to agriculture. Every household plants mango trees to form groves; although they share the same name, there are two varieties: the small ones are green when raw and yellow when ripe, while the large ones remain green from beginning to end. The country produces fine striped cotton cloth and gold. The climate is hot, and the customs are honest and compliant; the people delight in cultivating merit for the afterlife, and they revere virtue and value learning. There are more than twenty monasteries and over two thousand monks, who study both the Great and Lesser Vehicles with equal diligence. There are five *deva* temples, where followers of various heterodox sects live together. There are three *stūpas* that were all built by King Aśoka. There are many traces of the four past Buddhas. There are *stūpas* containing the relics of the holy disciples of the Śākya Tathāgata, namely: Śāriputra (formerly called Shelizi or Shelifu, which are erroneous abbreviations), Maudgalyāyana (formerly called Mujianlian, which is erroneous), Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra (called Manci Zi in the Tang language; formerly called Miduoluonizi, which is an erroneous abbreviation), Upāli, Ānanda, Rāhula (formerly called Luohou or Luoyun, both of which are erroneous abbreviations), and Mañjuśrī (called Miaojixiang [妙吉祥] in the Tang language; formerly called Rushou [濡首], also Wenshushili [文殊師利], or sometimes Manshushili [曼殊尸利], translated as 'Wonderful Virtue' [妙德], which is erroneous), and the stūpas of the various Bodhisattvas. During the three long fast months of every year and the six fast days of every month, the members of the Saṅgha compete with one another, leading those of like mind to bring offerings and prepare many rare curiosities, presenting them before the images of their respective patrons. Those who study the Abhidharma make offerings to Śāriputra; those who practice meditation make offerings to Maudgalyāyana; those who recite and uphold the Sūtras make offerings to Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra; those who study the Vinaya make offerings to Upāli; the various bhikṣuṇīs make offerings to Ānanda; those who have not yet received the full ordination make offerings to Rāhula; and those who study the Mahāyāna make offerings to the various Bodhisattvas. On these days, the various stūpas compete in performing offerings; pearl-adorned banners are arrayed in rows, precious canopies are lined up, smoke from incense is like clouds, and flowers are scattered like rain, obscuring the sun and moon and shaking the valleys. The king and his ministers make the cultivation of merit their primary duty.

zh: 城東行五六里，至一山伽藍，疎崖為室，因谷為門，尊者鄔波毱多（唐言近護）之所建也。其中則有如來指爪窣堵波。伽藍北巖間，有石室，高二十餘尺，廣三十餘尺，四寸細籌填積其內。尊者近護說法化導，夫妻俱證羅漢果者，乃下一籌，異室別族，雖證不記。石室東南二十四五里，至大涸池，傍有窣堵波。在昔如來行經此處，時有彌猴，持蜜奉佛，佛令水和，普遍大眾。獼猴喜躍，墮坑而死，乘茲福力，得生人中。池北不遠，大林中有過去四佛經行遺迹。其側有舍利子、沒特伽羅子等千二百五十大阿羅漢習定之處，並建窣堵波，以記遺迹。如來在世，屢遊此國，說法之所，並有封樹。
en_current: Traveling five or six *li* to the east of the city, one arrives at a mountain monastery where the cliffs were hollowed out to form chambers and the valleys were utilized as gateways; it was built by the Venerable Upagupta (in the language of the Tang, "Close Protector" [Jinhu]). Within it is a *stūpa* containing the finger-nails of the Tathāgata. In the cliffs to the north of the monastery, there is a stone chamber over twenty *chi* high and thirty *chi* wide, filled with fine bamboo tallies four *cun* in length. When the Venerable Close Protector preached the Dharma and provided guidance, whenever a husband and wife both attained the fruit of an Arhat, he would place one tally inside; those from different households or different clans, even if they attained the fruit, were not recorded. Twenty-four or twenty-five *li* to the southeast of the stone chamber, one reaches a large dried-up pond, beside which stands a *stūpa*. In the past, when the Tathāgata was traveling through this place, there was a monkey who brought honey to offer to the Buddha. The Buddha instructed him to mix it with water and distribute it to the great assembly. The monkey, leaping with joy, fell into a pit and died; by the power of this merit, he was reborn among humans. Not far to the north of the pond, in a large forest, are the remains of the places where the four Buddhas of the past walked in meditation. Beside them is the place where Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, and one thousand two hundred and fifty great Arhats practiced meditation; *stūpas* have been built at all these sites to mark the remains. While the Tathāgata was in the world, he frequently traveled through this country, and at the places where he preached the Dharma, mounds and trees have been established.

name_zh: 大涸池・獼猴奉蜜窣堵波
zh: 石室東南二十四五里，至大涸池，傍有窣堵波。在昔如來行經此處，時有彌猴，持蜜奉佛，佛令水和，普遍大眾。獼猴喜躍，墮坑而死，乘茲福力，得生人中。
en_current: Twenty-four or twenty-five li to the southeast of the stone chamber, one reaches a large dried-up pond, beside which stands a stūpa. In the past, when the Tathāgata was traveling through this place, there was a monkey who took honey and offered it to the Buddha. The Buddha ordered it to be mixed with water and distributed to the entire assembly. The monkey leaped with joy, fell into a pit, and died; by the power of this merit, it was reborn in the human realm.

zh: 從此東北行五百餘里，至薩他泥濕伐羅國（中印度境）。薩他泥濕伐羅國，周七千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。土地沃壤，稼穡滋盛。氣序溫暑，風俗澆薄，家室富饒，競為奢侈。深閑幻術，高尚異能。多逐利，少務農，諸方奇貨多聚其國。伽藍三所，僧徒七百餘人，並皆習學小乘法教。天祠百餘所，異道甚多。
en_current: From here, traveling northeast for more than five hundred li, one reaches the country of Sthāneśvara (薩他泥濕伐羅國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Sthāneśvara is more than seven thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than twenty li in circuit. The land is fertile and rich, and the crops are abundant. The climate is warm and hot. The customs are degenerate; the households are wealthy and prosperous, and they compete in being extravagant. They are deeply skilled in magical arts and highly esteem extraordinary abilities. They mostly pursue profit and pay little attention to farming; rare goods from various regions are mostly gathered in this country. There are three saṃghārāmas (伽藍) with more than seven hundred monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Hīnayāna. There are more than one hundred deva temples (天祠), and there are many heterodox sects.

zh: 大城四周二百里內，彼土之人謂為福地。聞諸先志曰：昔五印度國二王分治，境壤相侵，干戈不息。兩主合謀，欲決兵戰，以定雌雄，以寧氓俗。黎庶胥怨，莫從君命。王以為眾庶者，難與慮始也，神可動物，權可立功。時有梵志，素知高才，密齎束帛，命入後庭，造作法書，藏諸巖穴。歲月既久，樹皆合拱。王於朝坐，告諸臣曰：「吾以不德，忝居大位，天帝垂照，夢賜靈書，今在某山，藏於某嶺。」於是下令營求，得書山林之下。群官稱慶，眾庶悅豫，宣示遠近，咸使聞知。其大略曰：「夫生死無崖，流轉無極，含靈淪溺，莫由自濟。我以奇謀，令離諸苦。今此王城周二百里，古先帝世福利之地。歲月極遠，銘記堙滅，生靈不悟，遂沈苦海。溺而不救，夫何謂歟？汝諸含識，臨敵兵死，得生人中，多殺無辜，受天福樂，順孫孝子，扶侍親老，經遊此地，獲福無窮。功少福多，如何失利？一喪人身，三途冥漠。是故含生，各務修業！」於是人皆兵戰，視死如歸。王遂下令，招募勇烈，兩國合戰，積屍如莽。迄于今時，遺骸遍野，時既古昔，人骸偉大。國俗相傳，謂之福地。城西北四五里，有窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也。甎皆黃赤色，甚光淨，中有如來舍利一斗，光明時照，神迹多端。
en_current: Within a radius of two hundred li around the great city, the people of that land call it the Land of Blessedness (Kurukṣetra). According to the records of former times, the Five Indias were once ruled by two kings; their territories bordered each other and were subject to mutual invasions, with wars never ceasing. The two rulers conspired together, wishing to decide the matter through a decisive battle to determine the victor and bring peace to the populace. The common people were all resentful and would not follow the kings' commands. The kings thought that it is difficult to plan the beginning of an undertaking with the masses, but that the divine can move living beings and authority can establish merit. At that time, there was a Brahman known for his great talent; the king secretly presented him with a gift of silk and ordered him into the rear palace to compose a sacred text, which was then hidden in a mountain cave. As time passed, the trees grew to the size of a man’s embrace. The king sat in court and told his ministers: "Because of my lack of virtue, I unworthily occupy this high position; yet the Emperor of Heaven has looked down upon me and granted me a spiritual book in a dream, which is now located on a certain mountain, hidden on a certain ridge." Thereupon, he issued an order to search for it, and the book was found beneath the mountain forest. The officials offered congratulations, and the masses were joyful; it was proclaimed far and near, so that all might hear and know of it. Its general purport was: "Life and death are without bounds, and the cycle of transmigration is endless; sentient beings are submerged and drowning, with no way to save themselves. I, through a marvelous stratagem, shall cause them to depart from all suffering. Now, this royal city and its surroundings of two hundred li were a land of blessings and merit in the ages of former emperors. As the years and months have been extremely long, the inscriptions and records have been obliterated; living beings do not realize this and have consequently sunk into the sea of suffering. If they are drowning and not saved, what is to be said of it?" "All you sentient beings, if you die facing the enemy in battle, you will be reborn among humans; if you slaughter many of the innocent, you will receive the blessings and joys of heaven; and if obedient grandsons and filial sons who serve their elderly parents travel through this land, they shall obtain infinite blessings. With so little effort yielding such great merit, how could you let this advantage slip away? Once you lose this human body, the three paths (the three lower realms of existence) are dark and obscure. Therefore, let all living beings each apply themselves to their practice!" Thereupon, the people all engaged in battle, viewing death as a return home. The king then issued an order to recruit the brave and fierce; the two kingdoms joined in battle, and the piled-up corpses were like dense grass. Down to the present day, skeletal remains are scattered across the fields; as the events took place in ancient times, the human bones are of a massive size. Local custom passes down the name of this place as the Land of Blessings (Kurukṣetra). Four or five li to the northwest of the city, there is a stūpa over two hundred feet high, which was built by King Aśoka (無憂王). The bricks are all a yellowish-red color and are very bright and clean. Inside is one *dou* of the Tathāgata’s relics, which emit light from time to time and manifest many divine wonders.

zh: 城南行百餘里，至俱昏（去聲）荼僧伽藍。重閣連甍，層臺間峙。僧徒清肅，威儀閑雅。
en_current: Traveling more than one hundred li to the south of the city, one arrives at the Gukhunda (俱昏荼) (昏 in the departing tone) monastery. Multi-storied pavilions have connected roof ridges, and terraced platforms stand interspersed between them. The community of monks is pure and disciplined, and their deportment is calm and elegant.

zh: 城西北四五里，有窣堵波，高二百餘尺，無憂王之所建也。甎皆黃赤色，甚光淨，中有如來舍利一斗，光明時照，神迹多端。
en_current: Four or five li to the northwest of the city, there is a stūpa (窣堵波) over two hundred feet high, which was built by King Aśoka (無憂王). The bricks are all a yellowish-red color and are very bright and clean. Inside, there is one *dou* of the Tathāgata’s relics, which emit light from time to time and manifest many divine wonders.

zh: 從此東北行四百餘里，至窣祿勤那國（中印度境）。窣祿勤那國，周六千餘里，東臨殑伽河，北背大山，閻牟那河中境而流。國大都城周二十餘里，東臨閻牟那河，荒蕪雖甚，基趾尚固。土地所產，風氣所宜，同薩他泥濕伐羅國。人性淳質，宗信外道。貴藝學，尚福慧。伽藍五所，僧徒千餘人，多學小乘，少習餘部。商搉微言，清論玄奧，異方俊彥，尋論稽疑。天祠百所，異道甚多。大城東南閻牟那河西，大伽藍東門外，有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。如來在昔，曾於此處說法度人。其側又一窣堵波，中有如來髮、爪也。舍利子、沒特伽羅諸阿羅漢髮、爪窣堵波，周其左右，數十餘所。如來寂滅之後，此國為諸外道所詿誤焉，信受邪法，捐廢正見。今有五伽藍者，乃異國論師與諸外道及婆羅門論議勝處，因此建焉。
en_current: From here, traveling northeast for more than four hundred li, one arrives at the country of Srughna (窣祿勤那國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Srughna is over six thousand li in circuit; it borders the Ganges (gaṅgā) river to the east, rests against great mountains to the north, and the Yamunā river flows through the middle of its territory. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circuit; it borders the Yamunā river to the east. Although it is very desolate, its foundations remain firm. The produce of the land and the suitability of the climate are the same as in the country of Sthāneśvara (薩他泥濕伐羅國). The people are honest and simple by nature, and they revere and believe in non-Buddhist paths. They value the arts and sciences, and esteem both merit and wisdom. There are five monasteries with over one thousand monks, most of whom study the Lesser Vehicle (Hīnayāna), while few study other schools. They deliberate on subtle doctrines and engage in pure, profound discussions; talented scholars from distant regions come here to investigate doctrines and resolve doubts. There are one hundred Deva temples, and the non-Buddhist sects are very numerous. To the southeast of the great city, on the west bank of the Yamunā river and outside the eastern gate of a large monastery, there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka. In the past, the Tathāgata once preached the Dharma here to save people. Beside it is another stūpa, which contains the hair and nails of the Tathāgata. Surrounding it on the left and right are several dozen stūpas containing the hair and nails of the arhats Śāriputra (舍利子) and Maudgalyāyana (沒特伽羅). After the Tathāgata entered extinction, this country was misled by various non-Buddhists; they accepted and followed erroneous teachings and abandoned correct views. The five monasteries that exist today were built at the sites where masters from other countries held debates and emerged victorious over various non-Buddhists and Brahmins.

zh: 閻牟那河東行八百餘里，至殑伽河河源，廣三四里，東南流入海處廣十餘里。水色滄浪，波流浩汗，靈怪雖多，不為物害，其味甘美，細沙隨流。彼俗書記，謂之福水，罪咎雖積，沐浴便除；輕命自沈，生天受福；死而投骸，不墮惡趣；揚波激流，亡魂獲濟。時執師子國提婆菩薩深達實相，得諸法性，愍諸愚夫，來此導誘。當是時也，士女咸會，少長畢萃，於河之濱，揚波激流。提婆菩薩和光汲引，俯首反激，狀異眾人。有外道曰：「吾子何其異乎？」提婆菩薩曰：「吾父母親宗在執師子國，恐苦飢渴，冀斯遠濟。」諸外道曰：「吾子謬矣！曾不再思，妄行此事。家國綿邈，山川遼敻，激揚此水，給濟彼飢，其猶却行以求前及，非所聞也。」提婆菩薩曰：「幽途罪累，尚蒙此水；山川雖阻，如何不濟？」時諸外道知難謝屈，捨邪見，受正法，改過自新，願奉教誨。
en_current: Traveling over eight hundred *li* east from the Yamunā River, one reaches the source of the Ganges River (Gaṅgā), which is three or four *li* wide; where it flows southeast into the sea, it is over ten *li* wide. The color of the water is a deep blue, and the waves flow vast and wide. Although there are many spiritual anomalies, they do not harm living beings. Its taste is sweet and delicious, and fine sand flows along with the current. According to the records of the local customs, it is called the "water of merit." Even if one has accumulated sins and transgressions, bathing in it removes them. Those who hold life lightly and drown themselves are reborn in heaven and receive blessings; those who cast their remains into it after death do not fall into the evil paths; and by splashing the waves and agitating the current, the souls of the departed obtain salvation.  At that time, the Bodhisattva Deva (提婆菩薩) from the country of Siṃhala (執師子國) had deeply penetrated the true reality and attained the nature of all phenomena. Pitying these foolish people, he came here to guide and instruct them. At that time, men and women had all gathered, young and old alike, and were splashing the waves and agitating the current on the riverbank. The Bodhisattva Deva, mingling with them to draw the water, lowered his head and pushed the water in the opposite direction, his behavior differing from that of the crowd. A non-Buddhist asked, "Why are you acting so strangely, sir?" The Bodhisattva Deva replied, "My parents and relatives are in the country of Siṃhala. I fear they are suffering from hunger and thirst, and I hope to provide them with relief from afar." The non-Buddhists said, "You are mistaken, sir! You have not thought this through and are performing this act in vain. Your home and country are far away, separated by vast mountains and rivers; to splash this water here to relieve their hunger there is like walking backward to try and reach a destination in front—it is unheard of." The Bodhisattva Deva replied, "If those burdened by sins in the dark paths of the afterlife can still receive the benefit of this water, why should it not reach those separated by mountains and rivers?" At that time, the various non-Buddhists (外道), realizing that they were defeated by his logic, abandoned their false views, accepted the true Dharma, reformed themselves, and wished to follow his teachings.

zh: 渡河東岸至秣底補羅國（中印度境）。秣底補羅國，周六千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。宜穀、麥，多華果。氣序和暢，風俗淳質。崇尚學藝，深閑呪術。信邪正者，其徒相半。王，戍達羅種也，不信佛法，敬事天神。伽藍十餘所，僧徒八百餘人，多學小乘教說一切有部。天祠五十餘所，異道雜居。大城南四五里，至小伽藍，僧徒五十餘人。昔瞿拏鉢剌婆（唐言德光）論師於此作《辯真》等論，凡百餘部。論師少而英傑，長而弘敏，博物強識，碩學多聞。本習大乘，未窮玄奧，因覽《毘婆沙論》，退業而學小乘，作數十部論，破大乘綱紀，成小乘執著。又製俗書數十餘部，非斥先進所作典論。覃思佛經，十數不決，研精雖久，疑情未除。時有提婆犀那（唐言天軍）羅漢，往來覩史多天。德光願見慈氏，決疑請益。天軍以神通力，接上天宮。既見慈氏，長揖不禮。天軍謂曰：「慈氏菩薩次紹佛位，何乃自高，敢不致敬？方欲受業，如何不屈？」德光對曰：「尊者此言，誠為指誨。然我具戒苾芻，出家弟子，慈氏菩薩受天福樂，非出家之侶，而欲作禮，恐非所宜。」菩薩知其我慢心固，非聞法器，往來三返，不得決疑。更請天軍，重欲覲禮。天軍惡其我慢，蔑而不對。德光既不遂心，便起恚恨，即趣山林，修發通定，我慢未除，不證道果。德光伽藍北三四里，有大伽藍，僧徒二百餘人，並學小乘法教，是眾賢論師壽終之處。論師，迦濕彌羅國人也，聰敏博達，幼傳雅譽，特深研究《說一切有部毘婆沙論》。時有世親菩薩，一心玄道，求解言外，破毘婆沙師所執，作《阿毘達磨俱舍論》，辭義善巧，理致清高。眾賢循覽，遂有心焉。於是沈研鑽極，十有二歲，作《俱舍雹論》二萬五千頌，凡八十萬言矣。所謂言深致遠，窮幽洞微。告門人曰：「以我逸才，持我正論，逐斥世親，挫其鋒銳，無令老叟獨擅先名。」於是學徒四三俊彥，持所作論，推訪世親。世親是時在磔迦國奢羯羅城，遠傳聲問，眾賢當至。世親聞已，即治行裝。門人懷疑，前進諫曰：「大師德高先哲，名擅當時，遠近學徒莫不推謝。今聞眾賢，一何惶遽？必有所下，我曹厚顏。」世親曰：「吾今遠遊，非避此子。顧此國中，無復監達。眾賢後進也，詭辯若流，我衰耄矣，莫能持論。欲以一言頹其異執，引至中印度，對諸髦彥，察乎真偽，詳乎得失。」尋即命侶，負笈遠遊。眾賢論師當後一日至此伽藍，忽覺氣衰，於是裁書謝世親曰：「如來寂滅，弟子部執，傳其宗學，各擅專門，黨同道，疾異部。愚以寡昧，猥承傳習，覽所製《阿毘達磨俱舍論》，破毘婆沙師大義，輒不量力，沈究彌年，作為此論，扶正宗學。智小謀大，死其將至。菩薩宣暢微言，抑揚至理，不毀所執，得存遺文，斯為幸矣，死何悔哉？」於是歷選門人有辭辯者而告之曰：「吾誠後學，輕凌先達，命也如何？當從斯沒！汝持是書及所製論，謝彼菩薩，代我悔過。」授辭適畢，奄爾云亡。門人奉書至世親所而致辭曰：「我師眾賢已捨壽命。遺言致書，責躬謝咎。不墜其名，非所敢望。」世親菩薩覽書閱論，沈吟久之，謂門人曰：「眾賢論師聰敏後進，理雖不足，辭乃有餘。我今欲破眾賢之論，若指諸掌。顧以垂終之託，重其知難之辭，苟緣大義，存其宿志，況乎此論，發明我宗？」遂為改題為《順正理論》。門人諫曰：「眾賢未沒，大師遠迹，既得其論，又為改題，凡厥學徒，何顏受愧？」世親菩薩欲除眾疑，而說頌曰：「如師子王，避豕遠逝，二力勝負，智者應知。」眾賢死已，焚屍收骨，於伽藍西北二百餘步菴沒羅林中，起窣堵波，今猶現在。菴沒羅林側有窣堵波，毘末羅蜜多羅（唐言無垢友）論師之遺身。論師，迦濕彌羅國人也，於說一切有部而出家焉。博綜眾經，研究異論，遊五印度國，學三藏玄文，名立業成，將歸本國。途次眾賢論師窣堵波也，拊而歎曰：「惟論師雅量清高，抑揚大義，方欲挫異部，立本宗業也，如何降年不永！我無垢友猥承末學，異時慕義，曠代懷德。世親雖沒，宗學尚傳，我盡所知，當製諸論，令贍部洲諸學人等絕大乘稱，滅世親名，斯為不朽，用盡宿心。」說是語已，心發狂亂，五舌重出，熱血流涌。知命必終，裁書悔曰：「夫大乘教者，佛法之中究竟說也。名味泯絕，理致幽玄。輕以愚昧，駁斥先進，業報皎然，滅身宜矣。敢告學人，厥鑒斯在，各慎爾志，無得懷疑。」大地為震，命遂終焉。當其死處，地陷為坑。同旅焚屍，收骸旌建。時有羅漢見而歎曰：「惜哉！苦哉！今此論師，任情執見，毀惡大乘，墮無間獄。」
en_current: Crossing the river to the east bank, one arrives at the country of Matipura (秣底補羅國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Matipura is over six thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circuit. It is suitable for grain and wheat, and there are many flowers and fruits. The climate is harmonious and pleasant, and the customs are simple and honest. The people esteem learning and the arts, and are deeply skilled in magical incantations. Those who believe in heterodox paths and those who believe in the orthodox path are about equal in number. The king is of the Śūdra caste; he does not believe in the Buddha-Dharma and reverently serves the heavenly deities. There are more than ten monasteries with over eight hundred monks, most of whom study the Sarvāstivāda school of the Lesser Vehicle teachings. There are more than fifty temples to the heavenly deities, where followers of different paths live together. Four or five li to the south of the great city, one reaches a small monastery with over fifty monks. In the past, the master of treatises Guṇaprabha (in the Tang language, "Virtue-Light") composed the *Tattvavibhaṅga* (辯真) and other treatises here, totaling over one hundred works. The master of treatises was heroic and outstanding in his youth, and broad-minded and quick-witted in his maturity; he was widely learned and possessed a retentive memory, being a scholar of great erudition. Originally, he studied the Mahayana, but not having exhausted its profound mysteries, he read the *Vibhāṣā-śāstra* and subsequently abandoned his former studies to learn the Lesser Vehicle. He composed several dozen treatises, refuting the principles of the Mahayana and establishing the attachments of the Lesser Vehicle. He also produced several dozen secular books, criticizing and rejecting the canonical treatises composed by his predecessors. He pondered the Buddhist scriptures deeply, but there were over ten points he could not resolve; though he studied them with refinement for a long time, his doubts remained. At that time, there was an arhat named Devasena (in the Tang language, "Heavenly Army") who traveled back and forth to the Tuṣita Heaven. Guṇaprabha wished to see Maitreya to resolve his doubts and request further instruction. Devasena, using his supernatural powers, took him up to the heavenly palace. Upon seeing Maitreya (慈氏 - *Maitreya*), he merely made a long bow and did not prostrate. Devasena said to him, "Maitreya Bodhisattva is the next to succeed to the Buddha’s throne; why are you so arrogant that you dare not show him respect? You are seeking to receive instruction, so how can you not humble yourself?" Guṇaprabha (德光 - *Guṇaprabha*) replied, "Venerable one, your words are indeed a guide. However, I am a fully ordained bhikṣu and a monastic disciple, while Maitreya Bodhisattva enjoys the bliss of heavenly rewards and is not a member of the monastic order; I fear it would be inappropriate for me to pay him homage." The Bodhisattva, knowing that his pride was deeply rooted and that he was not a vessel fit to hear the Dharma, allowed him to travel back and forth three times without resolving his doubts. Guṇaprabha asked Devasena again, wishing to pay homage once more, but Devasena, disgusted by his pride, ignored him and did not reply. Since Guṇaprabha did not have his wish fulfilled, he harbored resentment and went into the mountain forests to practice meditation for the attainment of supernatural powers; however, because his pride was not eliminated, he did not realize the fruits of the Path.  Three or four *li* to the north of the Guṇaprabha monastery, there is a large monastery with over two hundred monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Lesser Vehicle (Hīnayāna). This is the place where the master of treatises Saṃghabhadra (眾賢 - *Saṃghabhadra*) passed away. The master of treatises was a man from the country of Kaśmīra (迦濕彌羅國 - *Kaśmīra*); he was intelligent and erudite, and from his youth he was renowned for his elegance, having studied the *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra* (說一切有部毘婆沙論) with particular depth. At that time, there was the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu (世親 - *Vasubandhu*), who was single-mindedly devoted to the profound Path and sought to understand the meaning beyond the words. He refuted the positions held by the masters of the *Vibhāṣā* and composed the *Abhidharmakośa-śāstra* (阿毘達磨俱舍論), in which the language and meaning were skillful and the principles were lofty and refined. Saṃghabhadra (眾賢) read it and was moved to action. Thereupon, he delved deeply into study and research for twelve years, composing the *Hailstone on the Kośa* (俱舍雹論) in twenty-five thousand verses, totaling eight hundred thousand words. It was said that his words were profound and his reach far, exhausting the hidden and penetrating the subtle. He told his disciples, "With my outstanding talent and upholding my correct arguments, I shall drive back Vasubandhu (世親) and blunt his sharp edge, so that the old man may no longer enjoy a monopoly on pre-eminent fame." Thereupon, three or four of his most talented disciples took the treatise he had written and went to seek out Vasubandhu. At that time, Vasubandhu was in the city of Sākala (奢羯羅城) in the country of Takka (磔迦國). Word was sent from afar that Saṃghabhadra was arriving. Upon hearing this, Vasubandhu immediately began to pack his belongings. His disciples, filled with doubt, came forward to remonstrate, saying, "Great Master, your virtue surpasses that of former sages and your fame is unrivaled in the present age; among students near and far, there are none who do not defer to you. Now, hearing of Saṃghabhadra, why are you so flustered? If you must yield to him, we will be deeply ashamed." Vasubandhu replied, "I am traveling far away now, not to avoid this man. It is just that in this country, there are no longer any discerning scholars. Saṃghabhadra is a younger scholar whose sophistry flows like a river; I am old and frail and cannot engage in debate. I wish to defeat his heterodox views with a single word and lead him to Central India to face the eminent and learned scholars, so that they may discern truth from falsehood and examine right and wrong." He immediately ordered his companions to pack their book-satchels and set out on the long journey. The Master of Treatises Saṃghabhadra (眾賢) arrived at this monastery one day later, when he suddenly felt his vitality failing. He then composed a letter to apologize to Vasubandhu (世親), saying: "Since the Thus-Come One passed into extinction, the disciples have held to their own sectarian views, each transmitting their own school's learning, each specializing in their own field, favoring those who share their path and disparaging those of different schools. In my ignorance and dullness, I rashly received these traditions. Upon reading the *Abhidharmakośa-śāstra* (阿毘達磨俱舍論) that you composed, which refutes the great principles of the Vaibhāṣika masters, I—without measuring my own strength—spent years in deep study and composed this treatise to uphold the orthodox school. My wisdom was small but my ambition was great, and now death is approaching. You, Bodhisattva, expound the subtle words and propagate the supreme truth; if you do not disparage my convictions and allow my writings to be preserved, I shall be fortunate indeed, and what regret could I have in death?" He then selected from among his disciples those who were eloquent and told them: "I am truly a junior scholar who has rashly insulted a senior master; such is my fate, what can be done? I am about to pass away. You must take this letter and the treatise I have composed, apologize to that Bodhisattva, and repent on my behalf." No sooner had he finished dictating these words than he suddenly passed away. The disciples took the letter to Vasubandhu and delivered the message, saying: "Our master Saṃghabhadra has already abandoned his life. He left a final letter to reproach himself and apologize for his faults. That his name not be forgotten is not something we would dare to hope for." Bodhisattva Vasubandhu read the letter and examined the treatise, and after pondering for a long time, he said to the disciples: "The Master of Treatises Saṃghabhadra was a clever junior; although his reasoning was insufficient, his rhetoric was more than enough. I now wish to refute Saṃghabhadra’s treatise, and it will be as easy as pointing to the palm of my hand." "However, considering his dying request and valuing his challenging words, if it serves the great principles, I shall preserve his original intention; furthermore, this treatise clarifies my own school." He then changed the title to the *Abhidharma-nyāyānusāra-śāstra* (Treatise Following the Correct Principles). His disciples remonstrated, saying: "While Saṃghabhadra was still alive, the Master withdrew far away; now that you have obtained his treatise, you even change its title for him—how can all the students face the shame of this?" Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, wishing to remove their doubts, spoke a verse: "Like a lion king, avoiding a boar and going far away, the wise should know the victory or defeat of the two powers." After Saṃghabhadra died, they cremated his body and collected his bones. In the Āmra (mango) grove, two hundred paces northwest of the monastery, they erected a stūpa, which still exists today. Beside the Āmra grove is a stūpa containing the remains of the master Vimalamitra (in Tang language, "Stainless Friend"). The master was a man of the country of Kaśmīra (迦濕彌羅國) and had renounced the household life in the Sarvāstivāda school. He extensively studied the various scriptures and researched heterodox treatises. He traveled through the five Indias, studied the profound texts of the Tripiṭaka, and having established his reputation and completed his work, he was about to return to his home country. Passing by the stūpa of the master Saṃghabhadra, he patted it and sighed, saying: "The master possessed such noble magnanimity and refined character, expounding the great principles; just as he was about to defeat the heterodox sects and establish the legacy of his own school, how is it that his years were not prolonged! I, Vimalamitra, humbly follow in his footsteps; I have long admired his righteousness and have cherished his virtue across the ages." "Although Vasubandhu (世親) has passed away, his school's teachings are still transmitted. I shall exhaust all my knowledge to compose various treatises, causing the scholars of Jambudvīpa (贍部洲) to abandon the name of the Mahāyāna and to efface the fame of Vasubandhu; this shall be my immortal achievement, fulfilling my long-held ambition." Having spoken these words, his mind became deranged, five tongues emerged from his mouth, and hot blood gushed forth. Knowing that his life was surely coming to an end, he composed a letter of repentance, saying: "The Mahāyāna teachings are the ultimate discourse within the Buddha-dharma. Their names and meanings are profound and absolute, and their principles are subtle and mysterious. Because of my ignorance, I lightly refuted these advanced teachings; the karmic retribution is clear, and it is fitting that my body should be destroyed. I dare to warn all students: take this as a lesson, guard your intentions, and do not harbor doubts." The great earth shook, and his life then ended. At the place where he died, the ground sank into a pit. His traveling companions cremated his corpse, collected the remains, and built a memorial over them. At that time, an Arhat (羅漢) saw this and sighed, saying: "Alas! How painful! This master of treatises, following his own emotions and holding to his views, slandered and disparaged the Mahāyāna, and has fallen into the Avīci (無間) hell."

zh: 國西北境殑伽河東岸有摩裕羅城，周二十餘里。居人殷盛，清流交帶，出鍮石、水精、寶器。去城不遠，臨殑伽河，有大天祠，甚多靈異。其中有池，編石為岸，引殑伽水為補，五印度人謂之殑伽河門，生福滅罪之所。常有遠方數百千人，集此澡濯。樂善諸王建立福舍，備珍羞，儲醫藥，惠施鰥寡，周給孤獨。
en_current: In the northwest territory of the kingdom, on the east bank of the Ganges (gaṅgā) River, lies the city of Mayūra (摩裕羅城), which is over twenty li in circuit. The inhabitants are prosperous, and the city is encircled by clear streams; it produces brass, rock crystal, and precious vessels. Not far from the city, bordering the Ganges River, there is a great deva temple with many miraculous manifestations. Within it is a pond with stone-lined banks, replenished by water diverted from the Ganges; the people of the five Indias call it the Gate of the Ganges (Gaṅgādvāra), a place for generating merit and expiating sins. Constantly, hundreds of thousands of people from distant regions gather here to bathe. Benevolent kings have established charitable hostels here, stocked with fine food and stored with medicines, to bestow gifts upon the widowed and solitary, and to provide for the orphaned and destitute.

zh: 大城南四五里，至小伽藍，僧徒五十餘人。昔瞿拏鉢剌婆（唐言德光）論師於此作《辯真》等論，凡百餘部。論師少而英傑，長而弘敏，博物強識，碩學多聞。本習大乘，未窮玄奧，因覽《毘婆沙論》，退業而學小乘，作數十部論，破大乘綱紀，成小乘執著。又製俗書數十餘部，非斥先進所作典論。覃思佛經，十數不決，研精雖久，疑情未除。時有提婆犀那（唐言天軍）羅漢，往來覩史多天。德光願見慈氏，決疑請益。天軍以神通力，接上天宮。既見慈氏，長揖不禮。天軍謂曰：「慈氏菩薩次紹佛位，何乃自高，敢不致敬？方欲受業，如何不屈？」德光對曰：「尊者此言，誠為指誨。然我具戒苾芻，出家弟子，慈氏菩薩受天福樂，非出家之侶，而欲作禮，恐非所宜。」菩薩知其我慢心固，非聞法器，往來三返，不得決疑。更請天軍，重欲覲禮。天軍惡其我慢，蔑而不對。德光既不遂心，便起恚恨，即趣山林，修發通定，我慢未除，不證道果。
en_current: Four or five li south of the great city, one arrives at a small monastery with over fifty monks. In the past, the master of treatises Guṇaprabha (known in Chinese as De Guang, "Virtue-Light") composed the *Bian zhen lun* (Treatise on Distinguishing the Truth) and other works here, over a hundred works in all. As a youth, the master was heroic and outstanding; as he grew older, he became broad-minded and quick-witted, possessing vast knowledge and a retentive memory, and was a scholar of great learning. He originally studied the Mahāyāna, but not having exhausted its profound mysteries, he read the *Vibhāṣā-śāstra* and subsequently abandoned his former studies to learn the Hīnayāna. He composed several dozen treatises to refute the principles of the Mahāyāna and establish Hīnayāna doctrines. He also authored several dozen secular works, criticizing and rejecting the treatises composed by his predecessors. He pondered the Buddhist scriptures deeply, yet there were over ten points he could not resolve; though he studied them with great refinement for a long time, his doubts remained. At that time, there was an arhat named Devasena (known in Chinese as Tian Jun, "Heavenly Army") who traveled to and from the Tuṣita Heaven. Guṇaprabha wished to see Maitreya to resolve his doubts and seek instruction. Devasena used his supernatural powers to take him up to the heavenly palace. Upon seeing Maitreya, he merely made a long bow and did not prostrate. Devasena said to him, "Maitreya Bodhisattva is the next to succeed to the Buddha's throne; why are you so arrogant that you dare not show him respect? You are about to receive instruction, so why do you not bow down?" Guṇaprabha replied, "Venerable one, your words are indeed a guide. However, I am a fully ordained bhikṣu and a monastic disciple, while the Bodhisattva Maitreya enjoys the bliss of heavenly rewards and is not a member of the monastic order; I fear it would be inappropriate for me to pay him homage." The Bodhisattva knew that his heart was firmly set on pride and that he was not a vessel capable of hearing the Dharma; Guṇaprabha went back and forth three times, yet could not resolve his doubts. He again requested Devasena (天軍) to go and pay respects once more, but Devasena, loathing his arrogance, treated him with contempt and did not respond. Since Guṇaprabha (德光) did not have his wishes fulfilled, he gave rise to resentment and immediately went to the mountain forests to practice and develop supernatural powers and meditative concentration; however, because his pride was not yet eliminated, he did not realize the fruits of the Path.

zh: 德光伽藍北三四里，有大伽藍，僧徒二百餘人，並學小乘法教，是眾賢論師壽終之處。論師，迦濕彌羅國人也，聰敏博達，幼傳雅譽，特深研究《說一切有部毘婆沙論》。時有世親菩薩，一心玄道，求解言外，破毘婆沙師所執，作《阿毘達磨俱舍論》，辭義善巧，理致清高。眾賢循覽，遂有心焉。於是沈研鑽極，十有二歲，作《俱舍雹論》二萬五千頌，凡八十萬言矣。所謂言深致遠，窮幽洞微。告門人曰：「以我逸才，持我正論，逐斥世親，挫其鋒銳，無令老叟獨擅先名。」於是學徒四三俊彥，持所作論，推訪世親。世親是時在磔迦國奢羯羅城，遠傳聲問，眾賢當至。世親聞已，即治行裝。門人懷疑，前進諫曰：「大師德高先哲，名擅當時，遠近學徒莫不推謝。今聞眾賢，一何惶遽？必有所下，我曹厚顏。」世親曰：「吾今遠遊，非避此子。顧此國中，無復監達。眾賢後進也，詭辯若流，我衰耄矣，莫能持論。欲以一言頹其異執，引至中印度，對諸髦彥，察乎真偽，詳乎得失。」尋即命侶，負笈遠遊。眾賢論師當後一日至此伽藍，忽覺氣衰，於是裁書謝世親曰：「如來寂滅，弟子部執，傳其宗學，各擅專門，黨同道，疾異部。愚以寡昧，猥承傳習，覽所製《阿毘達磨俱舍論》，破毘婆沙師大義，輒不量力，沈究彌年，作為此論，扶正宗學。智小謀大，死其將至。菩薩宣暢微言，抑揚至理，不毀所執，得存遺文，斯為幸矣，死何悔哉？」於是歷選門人有辭辯者而告之曰：「吾誠後學，輕凌先達，命也如何？當從斯沒！汝持是書及所製論，謝彼菩薩，代我悔過。」授辭適畢，奄爾云亡。門人奉書至世親所而致辭曰：「我師眾賢已捨壽命。遺言致書，責躬謝咎。不墜其名，非所敢望。」世親菩薩覽書閱論，沈吟久之，謂門人曰：「眾賢論師聰敏後進，理雖不足，辭乃有餘。我今欲破眾賢之論，若指諸掌。顧以垂終之託，重其知難之辭，苟緣大義，存其宿志，況乎此論，發明我宗？」遂為改題為《順正理論》。門人諫曰：「眾賢未沒，大師遠迹，既得其論，又為改題，凡厥學徒，何顏受愧？」世親菩薩欲除眾疑，而說頌曰：「如師子王，避豕遠逝，二力勝負，智者應知。」
en_current: Three or four li to the north of Guṇaprabha's (德光) monastery, there is a large monastery with over two hundred monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Hīnayāna. This is the place where the master of treatises Saṃghabhadra (眾賢) passed away. The master of treatises was a man from the country of Kaśmīra (迦濕彌羅國). He was intelligent, erudite, and widely learned, and from his youth, he was renowned for his elegance. He delved particularly deeply into the *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra* (說一切有部毘婆沙論) of the Sarvāstivāda school. At that time, there was the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu (世親), who focused his mind on the profound Way and sought to understand the meaning beyond the words. To refute the doctrines held by the Vibhāṣā masters, he composed the *Abhidharmakośa-śāstra* (阿毘達磨俱舍論), which was skillful in its language and meaning, and sublime in its reasoning. Saṃghabhadra read it and set his mind on [refuting] it. Thereupon, he immersed himself in study and rigorous inquiry for twelve years, composing the *Kośakarakā-śāstra* (俱舍雹論, “Hailstorm on the Kośa”) in twenty-five thousand verses, totaling eight hundred thousand words. It is said that his words were profound and his reasoning far-reaching, exhausting the hidden and penetrating the subtle. He told his disciples, "With my outstanding talent and by upholding my correct arguments, go and refute Vasubandhu to blunt his sharp edge, so that the old man may no longer enjoy a monopoly on pre-eminent fame." Thereupon, three or four of his most talented disciples took the treatise he had written and went to seek out Vasubandhu. At that time, Vasubandhu was in the city of Sākala (奢羯羅城) in the country of Takka (磔迦國). News spread from afar that Saṃghabhadra was coming. Upon hearing this, Vasubandhu immediately began to pack his belongings. His disciples were suspicious and came forward to remonstrate, saying, "The Master’s virtue is higher than that of the ancient sages, and your fame dominates the present age; students from near and far all defer to you. Now, upon hearing of Saṃghabhadra, why are you so flustered? If you must lower yourself, we will be deeply ashamed." Vasubandhu said, "I am traveling far away now, not to avoid this person. It is just that in this country, there are no longer any discerning scholars. Saṃghabhadra is a junior, yet his sophistry flows like a river; I am old and decrepit, and no longer able to engage in debate. I wish to collapse his heterodox views with a single word and lead him to Central India, to face the eminent and learned scholars, so that they may discern truth from falsehood and examine right from wrong." He immediately ordered his companions to pack their book-satchels and set out on the long journey.  Master Saṃghabhadra arrived at this monastery one day later. Suddenly feeling his vitality failing, he composed a letter to apologize to Vasubandhu, saying: "Since the Tathāgata passed into extinction, the disciples have formed sects, each transmitting their own school’s teachings, each specializing in their own tradition, favoring those of their own path and detesting those of different sects. Being ignorant and of shallow learning, I humbly received the traditional teachings. Having read the *Abhidharmakośa-śāstra* (阿毘達磨俱舍論) composed by you, which refutes the great principles of the Vaibhāṣika masters, I overreached my abilities and spent many years in deep research to compose this treatise to uphold the orthodox school. My wisdom was small but my ambition was great; now my death is imminent. You, Bodhisattva, expound the subtle words and propagate the supreme truth; if you do not disparage my convictions and allow my writings to be preserved, I shall be fortunate indeed, and what regret could I have in death?"  Thereupon, he selected from among his disciples one who was eloquent and told him: "I am truly a junior scholar who has lightly insulted a senior master; such is my fate, what can be done? I am about to pass away. You must take this letter and the treatise I have composed, apologize to that Bodhisattva, and repent for my transgressions on my behalf." As soon as he finished giving these instructions, he suddenly passed away. The disciple took the letter and went to the place of Vasubandhu (世親), where he delivered the message, saying: "My master, Saṃghabhadra (眾賢), has already abandoned his life. He left instructions to send this letter, to reproach himself and apologize for his faults. That his name not be forgotten is more than we dare hope for." The Bodhisattva Vasubandhu read the letter and examined the treatise; after pondering for a long time, he said to the disciple: "The master of treatises, Saṃghabhadra, was a brilliant junior scholar; though his reasoning was insufficient, his rhetoric was more than enough. I could now refute Saṃghabhadra’s treatise as easily as pointing to the palm of my hand. However, considering his deathbed entrustment and respecting his words acknowledging the difficulty of his task, I shall, for the sake of great righteousness, preserve his lifelong ambition—especially since this treatise actually elucidates my own school of thought." He then changed its title to the *Nyāyānusāra-śāstra* (順正理論). The disciple remonstrated, saying: "While Saṃghabhadra was still alive, you, Great Master, kept far away from him. Having obtained his treatise, you now change its title; how will all his students have the face to bear such shame?" The Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, wishing to dispel all doubts, spoke a verse: "Like a lion king, avoiding a pig and going far away; the wise should know the victory or defeat of the two powers."

zh: 眾賢死已，焚屍收骨，於伽藍西北二百餘步菴沒羅林中，起窣堵波，今猶現在。
en_current: After Saṃghabhadra (眾賢) died, his corpse was cremated and his bones were collected; in a mango grove (菴沒羅林) more than two hundred paces northwest of the monastery (伽藍), a stūpa was erected, which still exists today.

zh: 菴沒羅林側有窣堵波，毘末羅蜜多羅（唐言無垢友）論師之遺身。論師，迦濕彌羅國人也，於說一切有部而出家焉。博綜眾經，研究異論，遊五印度國，學三藏玄文，名立業成，將歸本國。途次眾賢論師窣堵波也，拊而歎曰：「惟論師雅量清高，抑揚大義，方欲挫異部，立本宗業也，如何降年不永！我無垢友猥承末學，異時慕義，曠代懷德。世親雖沒，宗學尚傳，我盡所知，當製諸論，令贍部洲諸學人等絕大乘稱，滅世親名，斯為不朽，用盡宿心。」說是語已，心發狂亂，五舌重出，熱血流涌。知命必終，裁書悔曰：「夫大乘教者，佛法之中究竟說也。名味泯絕，理致幽玄。輕以愚昧，駁斥先進，業報皎然，滅身宜矣。敢告學人，厥鑒斯在，各慎爾志，無得懷疑。」大地為震，命遂終焉。當其死處，地陷為坑。同旅焚屍，收骸旌建。時有羅漢見而歎曰：「惜哉！苦哉！今此論師，任情執見，毀惡大乘，墮無間獄。」
en_current: Beside the Āmra forest is a stūpa containing the remains of the śāstrin Vimalamitra (毘末羅蜜多羅; in Chinese, *Wugouyou*, "Stainless Friend"). The śāstrin was a man of the country of Kaśmīra (迦濕彌羅國) who renounced the world in the Sarvāstivāda school. He was broadly versed in the various scriptures and studied heterodox treatises. He traveled through the five Indias, studied the profound texts of the Tripiṭaka, and having established his reputation and completed his work, he prepared to return to his native country. Passing by the stūpa of the śāstrin Saṃghabhadra, he patted it and sighed, saying: "Only you, Master, possessed such noble magnanimity and refined character, expounding the great principles; just as you were about to defeat the heterodox sects and establish the legacy of our own school, why was your life not prolonged! I, Vimalamitra, though a lowly student of the later generation, have long admired your righteousness and cherished your virtue across the ages. Although Vasubandhu has passed away, his school of learning is still transmitted. I shall exhaust all my knowledge to compose various treatises, causing the students of Jambudvīpa to cease praising the Mahāyāna and to extinguish the name of Vasubandhu. This would be an immortal achievement, fulfilling my long-held intention."  Having spoken these words, his mind became deranged, five tongues emerged from his mouth, and hot blood gushed forth. Knowing that his life was surely coming to an end, he composed a letter of repentance, saying: "The Mahāyāna teaching is the ultimate discourse within the Buddha-dharma. Its names and meanings are profound and absolute, and its principles are subtle and mysterious. Because of my ignorance, I lightly refuted the ancients; the karmic retribution is clear, and it is fitting that my body should be destroyed. I dare to warn students: take this as a mirror, each of you be cautious in your intentions, and do not harbor doubts." The great earth shook, and he then expired. At the place where he died, the ground sank into a pit. His traveling companions cremated his corpse, collected the remains, and erected a memorial. At that time, an Arhat (阿羅漢) saw this and sighed, saying, "How regrettable! How painful! This master of treatises (論師), following his own inclinations and clinging to his views, slandered and disparaged the Great Vehicle (大乘), and has fallen into the Uninterrupted Hell (無間獄)."

zh: 從此北行三百餘里，至婆羅吸摩補羅國（北印度境）。婆羅吸摩補羅國，周四千餘里，山周四境。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛，家室富饒。土地沃壤，稼穡時播，出鍮石、水精。氣序微寒，風俗剛猛。少學藝，多逐利。人性獷烈，邪正雜信。伽藍五所，僧徒寡少。天祠十餘所，異道雜居。
en_current: From here, traveling north for over three hundred li, one reaches the country of Brahmapura (婆羅吸摩補羅國) (within the borders of North India). The country of Brahmapura is over four thousand li in circuit, and mountains surround its four borders. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous, and the households are wealthy. The soil is fertile, crops are sown in their proper seasons, and it produces brass and rock crystal. The climate is slightly cold, and the customs are fierce and unyielding. The people have little interest in the arts and are mostly driven by profit. Their nature is wild and violent, and they believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are five sanghārāmas, with few monks. There are more than ten deva temples, where followers of various heterodox paths live together.

zh: 此國境北大雪山中，有蘇伐剌拏瞿呾羅國（唐言金氏）。出上黃金，故以名焉。東西長，南北狹，即東女國也。世以女稱國。夫亦為王，不知政事，丈夫唯征伐，田種而已。土宜宿麥，多畜羊、馬。氣候寒烈，人性躁暴。東接吐蕃國，北接于闐國，西接三波訶國。
en_current: In the Great Snow Mountains to the north of this country lies the kingdom of Suvarṇagotra (translated into Chinese as the "Gold Clan"). It produces superior gold, and is named accordingly. It is long from east to west and narrow from north to south; this is the Eastern Women's Kingdom. For generations, the country has been named after women. The husband is also called king, but he does not manage state affairs; the men's only duties are warfare and farming. The soil is suitable for winter wheat, and there is an abundance of sheep and horses. The climate is cold and harsh, and the people are impetuous and violent. To the east it borders the kingdom of Tubo, to the north it borders the kingdom of Khotan, and to the west it borders the kingdom of Sampaha.

zh: 從末底補羅東南行四百餘里，至瞿毘霜那國（中印度境）。瞿毘霜那國，周二千餘里。國大都城周十四五里，崇峻險固，居人殷盛，華林池沼，往往相間。氣序土宜同末底補羅國。風俗淳質，勤學好福。多信外道，求現在樂。伽藍二所，僧眾百餘人，並皆習學小乘法教。天祠三十餘所，異道雜居。大城側故伽藍中，有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也，高二百餘尺。如來在昔，於此一月說諸法要，傍有過去四佛座及經行遺迹處。其側有如來髮、爪二窣堵波，各高一丈餘。
en_current: Traveling southeast from Matipura (末底補羅國) for more than four hundred li, one arrives at the country of Goviṣāṇa (瞿毘霜那國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Goviṣāṇa is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit; it is high, precipitous, and strategically secure, with a dense and prosperous population, and flowery groves and ponds are interspersed throughout. The climate and soil are the same as in the country of Matipura. The customs are simple and honest, and the people are diligent in learning and fond of merit. Many believe in non-Buddhist paths and seek present-day happiness. There are two saṃghārāmas with over one hundred monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Lesser Vehicle (Hīnayāna). There are more than thirty Deva temples, where followers of various paths live together. Beside the old saṃghārāma near the great city, there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王) that is over two hundred feet high. In the past, the Tathāgata stayed here for one month to preach the essential Dharma; nearby are the seats and walking paths of the four past Buddhas. Beside these are two stūpas containing the hair and nail clippings of the Tathāgata, each over one zhang high.

zh: 自此東南行四百餘里，至堊醯掣呾邏國（中印度境）。堊醯掣呾邏國，周三千餘里。大都城周十七八里，依據險固，宜穀、麥，多林泉。氣序和暢，風俗淳質。翫道篤學，多才博識。伽藍十餘所，僧徒千餘人，習學小乘正量部法。天祠九所，異道三百餘人，事自在天，塗灰之侶也。城外龍池側有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。是如來在昔為龍王，七日於此說法。其側有四小窣堵波，是過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。
en_current: From here, traveling southeast for more than four hundred li, one reaches the country of Ahicchattra (堊醯掣呾邏國) (in the region of Central India). The country of Ahicchattra is more than three thousand li in circuit. The capital city is seventeen or eighteen li in circuit; it is situated in a secure and rugged position, is suitable for grain and wheat, and has many forests and springs. The climate is temperate and pleasant, and the customs of the people are honest and simple. They delight in the Way and are diligent in their studies, being talented and widely learned. There are more than ten sanghārāmas (伽藍) and over one thousand monks, who study the teachings of the Sammatiya school (正量部) of the Lesser Vehicle. There are nine deva temples, and more than three hundred sectarians who serve Īśvara (自在天) and are followers of the ash-smearing ascetics. Outside the city, beside a dragon pool, there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王). It was here that the Tathāgata, in a former life when he was a dragon king, preached the Dharma for seven days. Beside it are four small stūpas, which are the sites of the remains of the seats and walking paths of the four past Buddhas.

zh: 城外龍池側有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。是如來在昔為龍王，七日於此說法。其側有四小窣堵波，是過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。
en_current: Outside the city, beside the dragon pond, there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王). It was here that the Tathāgata, in a former life as a dragon king, preached the Dharma for seven days. Beside it are four small stūpas, which are the sites marking the places where the four past Buddhas sat and performed walking meditation.

zh: 自此東行二百六七十里，渡殑伽河，南至毘羅那拏國（中印度境）。毘羅那拏國，周二千餘里。國大都城周十餘里。氣序土宜，同堊醯掣呾邏國。風俗猛暴，人知學藝。崇信外道，少敬佛法。伽藍二所，僧徒三百人，並皆習學大乘法教。天祠五所，異道雜居。大城中故伽藍內，有窣堵波基，雖傾圮，尚百餘尺，無憂王之所建也。如來在昔於此七日說《蘊界處經》之所。其側則有過去四佛座及經行遺迹斯在。
en_current: From here, traveling east for two hundred sixty or seventy li and crossing the Ganges (Gaṅgā) River, one arrives south at the country of Vilaśāṇa (毘羅那拏國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Vilaśāṇa is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is over ten li in circuit. The climate and soil conditions are the same as those of the country of Ahicchatrā (堊醯掣呾邏國). The customs of the people are fierce and violent, yet they are knowledgeable in the arts. They revere and believe in non-Buddhist paths and have little respect for the Buddha-Dharma. There are two monasteries with three hundred monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Great Vehicle. There are five Deva temples where followers of various non-Buddhist paths live together. Inside an old monastery in the great city, there is the base of a stūpa which, although dilapidated, is still over one hundred feet high; it was built by King Aśoka. This is the place where the Tathāgata in the past spent seven days preaching the *Skandhadhātvāyatana-sūtra* (蘊界處經). Beside it are the seats and traces of the walking paths of the four past Buddhas.

zh: 從此東南行二百餘里，至劫比他國（舊謂僧迦舍國。中印度境）。劫比他國，周二千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。氣序土宜，同毘羅那拏國。風俗淳和，人多學藝。伽藍四所，僧徒千餘人，並學小乘正量部法。天祠十所，異道雜居，同共遵事大自在天。
en_current: From here, traveling southeast for more than two hundred li, one reaches the country of Kapitha (劫比他國) (the old name is the country of Saṃkāśya; it is within the borders of Central India). The country of Kapitha is more than two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than twenty li in circuit. The climate and soil conditions are the same as those of the country of Viraṇāṇa (毘羅那拏國). The customs are honest and harmonious, and the people are mostly devoted to learning and the arts. There are four saṃghārāmas with more than one thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Hīnayāna Saṃmitīya school. There are ten deva temples where followers of different paths live together, all of whom jointly worship Maheśvara.

zh: 城西二十餘里有大伽藍，經製輪奐，工窮剞劂，聖形尊像，務極莊嚴。僧徒數百人，學正量部法。數萬淨人，宅居其側。伽藍大垣內有三寶階，南北列，東面下，是如來自三十三天降還也。昔如來起自勝林，上昇天宮，居善法堂，為母說法，過三月已，將欲下降。天帝釋乃縱神力，建立寶階，中階黃金，左水精，右白銀。如來起善法堂，從諸天眾，履中階而下；大梵王執白拂，履銀階而右侍；天帝釋持寶蓋，蹈水精階而左侍；天眾凌虛，散華讚德。數百年前，猶有階級，逮至今時，陷沒已盡。諸國君王悲慨不遇，疊以塼石，飾以珍寶，於其故基，擬昔寶階，其高七十餘尺，上起精舍。中有石佛像，而左右之階有釋、梵之像，形擬厥初，猶為下勢。傍有石柱，高七十餘尺，無憂王所建。色紺光潤，質堅密理，上作師子，蹲踞向階，雕鏤奇形，周其方面，隨人罪福，影現柱中。寶階側不遠有窣堵波，是過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。其側窣堵波，如來在昔於此澡浴。其側精舍，是如來入定之處。精舍側有大石，基長五十步，高七尺，是如來經行之處。足所履迹皆有蓮華之文。基左右各有小窣堵波，帝釋、梵王之所建也。釋、梵窣堵波前，是蓮華色苾芻尼欲先見佛，化作轉輪王處。如來自天宮還贍部洲也，時蘇部底（唐言善現。舊曰須扶提，或曰須菩提，譯曰善吉，皆訛也）宴坐石室，竊自思曰：「今佛還降，人、天導從，如我今者，何所宜行？甞聞佛說，知諸法空，體諸法性，是則以慧眼觀法身也。」時蓮華色苾芻尼欲初見佛，化為轉輪王，七寶導從，四兵警衛，至世尊所，復苾芻尼。如來告曰：「汝非初見。夫善現者，觀諸法空，是見法身。」聖迹垣內，靈異相繼。其大窣堵波東南有一池龍，恒護聖迹。既有冥衛，難以輕犯，歲久自壞，人莫能毀。從此東南行，減二百里，至羯若鞠闍國（唐言曲女城國。中印度境）。
en_current: More than twenty *li* west of the city is a large monastery, its construction magnificent and its craftsmanship exquisite; the sacred forms and venerable images are adorned with the utmost solemnity. There are several hundred monks who study the teachings of the Saṃmitīya school, and tens of thousands of monastery servants (淨人) reside in its vicinity. Within the great wall of the monastery are the three precious stairways (三寶階), arranged from north to south and facing east, where the Tathāgata returned from the Trāyastriṃśa heaven. In the past, the Tathāgata rose from the Jetavana (勝林) and ascended to the heavenly palace, where he resided in the Hall of Good Dharma (Sudharmā-sabhā) to preach the Dharma for his mother. After three months had passed, he intended to descend. Śakra, the Lord of Devas, then exercised his divine power to establish a precious stairway: the middle step was of gold, the left of crystal, and the right of silver. The Tathāgata rose from the Hall of Good Dharma and, followed by a host of deities, stepped down the middle stairway; the Great Brahmā King, holding a white whisk, walked on the silver stairway to attend on the right; Śakra, the Lord of Devas, holding a precious canopy, stepped on the crystal stairway to attend on the left; the heavenly host hovered in the void, scattering flowers and praising his virtues. Several hundred years ago, the stairs still existed, but by the present time, they have completely sunk into the earth. The kings of various countries, lamenting that they could not see them, stacked bricks and stones and decorated them with precious gems upon the original foundation to imitate the ancient precious stairway. It is over seventy feet high, and a *vihāra* (精舍) is built upon it. Inside is a stone Buddha image, and on the stairs to the left and right are images of Śakra and Brahmā, modeled after the original appearance, still in a descending posture. Beside it is a stone pillar, over seventy feet high, erected by King Aśoka (無憂王). Its color is dark blue and lustrous, its substance hard and fine-grained. At the top is a lion, crouching and facing the stairway, with strange forms carved and engraved around its four sides; according to the merit or demerit of the person, shadows appear within the pillar. Not far from the precious stairway is a stūpa, which is the site of the traces where the four past Buddhas sat and performed walking meditation. Beside it is a stūpa where the Tathāgata formerly bathed. Beside that is a *vihāra* (精舍), which is the place where the Tathāgata entered into meditation. Beside the *vihāra* is a large stone, fifty paces long and seven feet high, which is the place where the Tathāgata performed walking meditation. The footprints he trod upon all have lotus patterns. To the left and right of the base are small stūpas, built by Śakra (帝釋) and Brahmā (梵王). In front of the stūpas of Śakra and Brahmā is the place where the bhikṣuṇī Utpalavarṇā (蓮華色), wishing to be the first to see the Buddha, transformed herself into a wheel-turning king. When the Tathāgata returned from the heavenly palace to Jambudvīpa, at that time Subhūti (蘇部底) (in the Tang language, Shanxian, 'Good Manifestation'; formerly called Xufuti [須扶提] or Xuputi [須菩提], translated as Shanji [善吉], 'Good Auspicious', all of which are erroneous) was sitting in meditation in a stone chamber and thought to himself: "Now the Buddha is descending, guided and followed by humans and devas. As for someone like me, what is appropriate to do?
