With the great assembly surrounding me, how am I different from the Tathāgata?" Having thought this, he proceeded to cause a schism in the Sangha. Śāriputra (舍利子) and Maudgalyāyana (沒特伽羅子), following the Buddha’s instructions and relying on the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, preached and admonished them, and the Sangha was reconciled. Devadatta did not abandon his evil heart; he placed a deadly poison under his fingernails, intending to harm the Buddha while performing an act of homage. As he was carrying out this plot, coming from afar and arriving at this spot, the earth suddenly split open, and he fell alive into hell. To the south of this, there is another large pit where the Bhikṣu Kokālika (瞿伽梨) fell alive into hell for slandering the Tathāgata. More than eight hundred paces to the south of the pit of Kokālika, there is a large, deep pit, which is the place where the Brahmin woman Ciñcā (戰遮) fell alive into hell for slandering the Tathāgata. When the Buddha was preaching the essentials of the Dharma to humans and devas, a disciple of an external path saw from afar the great assembly paying homage to the World-Honored One and thought to herself, "I must humiliate Gautama (喬答摩) today and ruin his good reputation, so that my teacher alone may possess a fragrant name." She then concealed a wooden basin tied to her body and went to the Jetavana (給孤獨園), where she cried out in a loud voice amidst the great assembly, "This preacher has had illicit relations with me, and the child in my womb is of the Śākya clan." Those of evil views all believed it to be true, while those who were steadfast knew it to be a slander. At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra (天帝釋), wishing to dispel the doubt, transformed into a white mouse and gnawed through the cord holding the basin. The sound of the cord snapping startled the great assembly, and all who saw and heard it felt their joy increase. One person in the assembly stood up, held the wooden basin, and showed it to the woman, saying, "Is this your child?" At that moment, the earth split open of its own accord, and she fell into it, her whole body sinking into the Avīci (無間) hell to suffer the full consequences of her actions. These three pits are bottomless; during the heavy rains of autumn and summer, when ditches and pools overflow, no water ever remains in these deep hollows. Sixty or seventy paces to the east of the monastery, there is a vihāra (精舍) over sixty feet high, in which there is an image of the Buddha seated facing east. In the past, the Tathāgata debated with various heretics here. To the east, there is a deva temple equal in size to the monastery. When the sun rises and sheds its light, the shadow of the deva temple does not cover the monastery; when the sun is about to set, the shadow of the monastery covers the deva temple. Three or four li to the east of the Shadow-covering Vihāra (影覆精舍), there is a stūpa, which is the place where the Venerable Śāriputra debated with the heretics.  Initially, the elder Sudatta (善施長者) purchased the garden of Prince Jeta (逝多太子) and wished to build a monastery for the Tathāgata. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra accompanied the elder to survey the site. The teachers of the six heretical schools sought to compete in supernatural powers, but Śāriputra converted them according to the circumstances and subdued them in response to their challenges. Beside it, in front of a vihāra, a stūpa has been built; here the Tathāgata defeated the various heretics and also accepted the invitation of Mother Viśākhā.  To the south of the stūpa where he accepted the invitation is the place where King Virūḍhaka (毘盧釋迦王) (formerly called King Piliuli (毘琉離主), which is incorrect) raised an army to slaughter the Śākya clan, and where he saw the Buddha and turned his troops back. After King Virūḍhaka ascended the throne, he pursued his resentment over a previous humiliation, raised an army, and mobilized the masses. Once the deployment was complete, he issued the order to march. At that time, a bhikṣu heard of this and informed the Buddha. The World-Honored One then sat beneath a withered tree. King Virūḍhaka saw the World-Honored One from afar, dismounted to pay his respects, stood back, and said, "Lush trees are spreading and thick; why do you not sit under them, but instead stay by a withered stump and rotten branches?" The World-Honored One replied, "One's own kin are like the branches and leaves. When the branches and leaves are in danger, where is the shade?" The King said, "The World-Honored One is doing this for his kinsmen; I may turn back my carriage." Thereupon, seeing the Holy One and feeling moved, he returned his army to his country. Beside the place where the army turned back, there is a stūpa, which is the place where the Śākya women were slaughtered. When King Virūḍhaka (毘盧釋迦王) had conquered the Śākyas, he selected five hundred women to fill his palace. The Śākya women were filled with indignation and, speaking resentful and insolent words, cursed the King, saying, "You are the son of a domestic servant." When the King heard this, he became enraged and ordered them to be slaughtered. The executioners obeyed the King’s command, severed their hands and feet, and threw them into a pit. At that time, the Śākya women, enduring their suffering, called upon the Buddha. The World-Honored One, with his holy insight, perceived their bitter agony and commanded the bhikṣus to gather their robes and go there. He preached the subtle Dharma to the Śākya women, explaining how they were bound by the five desires, wandering through the three evil paths, separated from those they loved, and caught in the long cycle of birth and death. When the Śākya women heard the Buddha’s instruction, they cast off the dust and removed the stains, attained the pure Dharma-eye, and at that same moment passed away and were all reborn in the heavens. At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra transformed himself into a Brahmin, collected their remains, and cremated them; later generations have commemorated this. Not far from the stūpa of the slaughtered Śākyas, there is a large dried-up pond, which is the place where King Virūḍhaka sank into the earth and fell into hell. After the World-Honored One had observed the Śākya women, he returned to the Jetavana (給孤獨園) and told the bhikṣus, "Seven days from now, King Virūḍhaka will be consumed by fire." When the King heard the Buddha’s prophecy, he was filled with great fear and anxiety. When the seventh day arrived, he was safe and without danger. The king, feeling jubilant, ordered the palace maidens to go to the riverside to enjoy themselves with music and wine. Still fearing that a fire might break out, he rowed upon the clear currents and drifted along with the waves. Suddenly, a blazing fire erupted, consuming the light boat; the king’s body fell, and he entered the Avīci Hell to undergo all manner of suffering.

zh: 伽藍西北三四里，至得眼林。有如來經行之迹，諸聖習定之所，並樹封記，建窣堵波。昔此國群盜五百，橫行邑里，跋扈城國。勝軍王捕獲已，抉去其眼，棄於深林。群盜苦逼，求哀稱佛。是時如來在逝多精舍，聞悲聲，起慈心，清風和暢，吹雪山藥，滿其眼已，尋得復明。而見世尊在其前住，發菩提心，歡喜頂禮，投杖而去，因植根焉。
en_current: Three or four li to the northwest of the monastery, one reaches the Wood of Regained Sight (Andhavana). There are traces of the Tathāgata’s walking meditation and places where various sages practiced concentration, all marked by commemorative signs, with stūpas built. In the past, there was a band of five hundred bandits in this country who ran amok in the villages and acted lawlessly throughout the cities and states. King Prasenajit (勝軍王) captured them, gouged out their eyes, and abandoned them in the deep forest. The bandits, tormented by suffering, cried out in supplication to the Buddha. At that time, the Tathāgata was in the Jetavana Monastery (逝多精舍); hearing their cries of grief, he felt great compassion, and a gentle, cooling breeze blew medicinal herbs from the Snow Mountains into their eyes, whereupon their sight was immediately restored. Upon seeing the World-Honored One standing before them, they conceived the resolve for enlightenment, bowed in joyful worship, and departed after casting down their staves, which then took root there.

zh: 大城西北六十餘里，有故城，是賢劫中人壽二萬歲時，迦葉波佛本生城也。城南有窣堵波，成正覺已初見父處。城北有窣堵波，有迦葉波佛全身舍利。並無憂王所建也。
en_current: More than sixty li to the northwest of the great city, there is an ancient city; this was the birthplace of the Buddha Kāśyapa (迦葉波佛) during the Bhadrakalpa, when the human lifespan was twenty thousand years. To the south of the city is a stūpa, which marks the place where he first met his father after attaining perfect enlightenment. To the north of the city is a stūpa containing the entire-body relics of the Buddha Kāśyapa. Both were built by King Aśoka (無憂王).

zh: 故宮城內有故基，勝軍王殿餘趾也。
en_current: Within the old palace city are ancient foundations, which are the remaining traces of the palace of King Prasenajit (勝軍王).

zh: 次東不遠，有一故基，上建小窣堵波，昔勝軍王為如來所建大法堂也。
en_current: Not far to the east, there is an old foundation upon which a small stūpa has been built; this is the site of the Great Dharma Hall (Mahādharmaśālā) that King Prasenajit (勝軍王) built for the Tathāgata in the past.

zh: 法堂側不遠，故基上有窣堵波，是佛姨母鉢邏闍鉢底（唐言生主。舊云波闍波提，訛也）苾芻尼精舍，勝軍王之所建立。
en_current: Not far from the side of the Dharma Hall, there is a stūpa on the old foundations, which is the *vihāra* (精舍) of the Buddha’s maternal aunt, the bhikṣuṇī Prajāpatī (鉢邏闍鉢底; in Chinese, *Shengzhu* [Lord of Beings]; the old form Bozhebodi 波闍波提 is erroneous), established by King Prasenajit (勝軍王).

zh: 次東窣堵波，是蘇達多（唐言善施。舊曰須達，訛也）故宅也。
en_current: To the east is a stūpa, which is the former residence of Sudatta (in Chinese, *Shànshī* [Well-Bestowing]; the old name *Xūdá* [Sudatta] is a corruption).

zh: 善施長者宅側有大窣堵波，是鴦窶利摩羅（唐言指鬘。舊曰央掘摩羅，訛也）捨邪之處，鴦窶利摩羅者，室羅伐悉底之凶人也。作害生靈，為暴城國，殺人取指，冠首為鬘。將欲害母，以充指數。世尊悲愍，方行導化。遙見世尊，竊自喜曰：「我今生天必矣。先師有教，遺言在茲，害佛殺母，當生梵天。」謂其母曰：「老今且止，先當害彼大沙門。」尋即杖劍往逆世尊。如來於是徐行而退，凶人指鬘疾驅不逮。世尊謂曰：「何守鄙志，捨善本，激惡源？」時指鬘聞誨，悟所行非，因即歸命，求入法中，精勤不怠，證羅漢果。
en_current: Beside the residence of the elder Anāthapiṇḍada (善施) is a large stūpa; this is the place where Aṅgulimāla (鴦窶利摩羅; in Tang language [Chinese] this means "Garland of Fingers"; the old translation "Yangjuemolu" is incorrect) abandoned his evil ways. Aṅgulimāla was a violent man of Śrāvastī (室羅伐悉底). He harmed living beings and committed atrocities throughout the city and country, killing people to take their fingers and wearing them on his head as a garland. He was about to kill his mother to complete the count of fingers. The World-Honored One, out of compassion, set out to guide and transform him. Seeing the World-Honored One from afar, he secretly rejoiced, saying to himself, "I shall certainly be reborn in the heavenly realm now. My former teacher gave me instructions, and his legacy is here: by harming a Buddha and killing one's mother, one shall be reborn in the Brahmā heaven." He said to his mother, "Old woman, stop for now; I must first kill that great śramaṇa." He immediately took up his sword and went to intercept the World-Honored One. The Tathāgata then retreated at a slow pace, yet the wicked Aṅgulimāla could not catch up even though he ran fast. The World-Honored One said to him, "Why do you persist in your base intentions, abandoning the root of goodness and inciting the source of evil?" At that time, Aṅgulimāla heard the instruction and realized that his actions were wrong. He then took refuge, sought to enter the Dharma, practiced with diligence and without sloth, and attained the fruit of an Arhat.

zh: 從此東南行五百餘里，至劫比羅伐窣堵國（舊曰迦羅衛國，訛。中印度境）。劫比羅伐窣堵國，周四千餘里。空城十數，荒蕪已甚。王城頹圮，周量不詳。其內宮城周十四五里，壘甎而成，基跡峻固。空荒久遠，人里稀曠。無大君長，城各立主。土地良沃，稼穡時播。氣序無愆，風俗和暢。伽藍故基千有餘所，而宮城之側有一伽藍，僧徒三千餘人，習學小乘正量部教。天祠兩所，異道雜居。宮城內有故基，淨飯王正殿也。上建精舍，中作王像。其側不遠有故基，摩訶摩耶（唐言大術）夫人寢殿也。上建精舍，中作夫人之像。其側精舍，是釋迦菩薩降神母胎處，中作菩薩降神之像。上座部菩薩以嗢呾羅頞沙荼月三十日夜降神母胎，當此五月十五日；諸部則以此月二十三日夜降母胎，當此五月八日。菩薩降神東北，有窣堵波，阿私多仙相太子處。菩薩誕靈之日，嘉祥輻湊。時淨飯王召諸相師而告之曰：「此子生也，善惡何若？宜悉乃正，明言以對。」曰：「依先聖之記，考吉祥之應，在家作轉輪聖王，捨家當成等正覺。」是時阿私多仙自遠而至，叩門請見。王甚慶悅，躬迎禮敬，請就寶座，曰：「不意大仙今日降顧。」仙曰：「我在天宮安居宴坐，忽見諸天群從蹈舞，我時問言：『何悅豫之甚也？』曰：『大仙當知，贍部洲中釋種淨飯王第一夫人，今產太子，當證三菩提，圓明一切智。』我聞是語，故來瞻仰。所悲朽耄，不遭聖化。」城南門有窣堵波，是太子與諸釋角力擲象之處。太子伎藝多能，獨拔倫匹。淨飯大王懷慶將返，僕夫馭象，方欲出城。提婆達多素負強力，自外而入，問馭者曰：「嚴駕此象，其誰欲乘？」曰：「太子將還，故往奉馭。」提婆達多發憤引象，批其顙，蹴其臆，僵仆塞路，杜絕行途，無能轉移，人眾填塞。難陀後至，而問之曰：「誰死此象？」曰：「提婆達多。」即曳之避路。太子至，又問曰：「誰為不善，害此象耶？」曰：「提婆達多害以杜門，難陀引之開徑。」太子乃舉象高擲，越度城塹，其象墮地，為大深阬，土俗相傳為象墮阬也。其側精舍中作太子像。其側又有精舍，太子妃寢宮也，中作耶輸陀羅，并有羅怙羅像。宮側精舍作受業之像，太子學堂故基也。城東南隅有一精舍，中作太子乘白馬凌虛之像，是踰城處也。城四門外各有精舍，中作老、病、死人、沙門之像。是太子遊觀，覩相增懷，深厭塵俗，於此感悟，命僕迴駕。
en_current: From here, traveling southeast for more than five hundred *li*, one arrives at the country of Kapilavastu (劫比羅伐窣堵國) (formerly called Jialuowei (迦羅衛國), which is incorrect; it is within the borders of Central India). The country of Kapilavastu is over four thousand *li* in circuit. There are more than ten empty cities, which are extremely desolate and overgrown. The royal city is in ruins, and its exact dimensions are unknown. The inner palace city is fourteen or fifteen *li* in circuit; it was built of piled bricks, and its foundations remain high and solid. Having been desolate for a long time, the inhabited villages are sparse and wide apart. There is no great monarch; each city has its own ruler. The land is fertile and rich, and crops are sown at the proper times. The climate is regular, and the customs are harmonious and pleasant. There are more than a thousand old foundations of *saṃghārāmas*, and beside the palace city is one *saṃghārāma* with more than three thousand monks who study the teachings of the Hīnayāna Saṃmitīya school. There are two *deva* temples; followers of different sects live intermixed.  Inside the palace city are the old foundations of the main hall of King Śuddhodana. A vihāra (精舍) has been built upon it, containing a statue of the king. Not far to its side are the old foundations of the bedchamber of Queen Mahāmāyā (which in Chinese means "Great Illusion"). A vihāra has been built upon it, containing a statue of the queen. The vihāra beside it is the place where the Bodhisattva Śākya descended into his mother’s womb; inside is a statue of the Bodhisattva descending into the womb. The Sthavira school holds that the Bodhisattva descended into his mother’s womb on the night of the thirtieth day of the month of Uttarāṣāḍhā, which corresponds to the fifteenth day of the fifth month here; the other schools hold that he descended into his mother’s womb on the night of the twenty-third day of that month, which corresponds to the eighth day of the fifth month here. To the northeast of the place where the Bodhisattva’s spirit descended, there is a stūpa at the site where the rishi Asita (阿私多) examined the physiognomy of the prince. On the day the Bodhisattva was born, auspicious signs converged. At that time, King Śuddhodana (淨飯王) summoned the various physiognomists and said to them: "This child has been born; what is his fortune, good or evil? You must examine him thoroughly and speak clearly in your reply." They said: "According to the records of the ancient sages and examining the auspicious omens, if he remains in household life, he will become a wheel-turning sage king (cakravartin); if he leaves the household life, he will attain equal and correct enlightenment (samyaksambodhi)." At this time, the rishi Asita arrived from afar and knocked at the gate to request an audience. The king was very joyful, personally welcomed and paid homage to him, and invited him to take a precious seat, saying: "I did not expect the great rishi to visit today." The rishi said: "I was dwelling in peace and sitting at ease in the heavenly palace when I suddenly saw the hosts of devas dancing. I then asked them: 'Why are you so extremely joyful?' They replied: 'Great rishi, you should know that in Jambudvīpa, the first wife of the Śākya King Śuddhodana has now given birth to a prince who shall attain *saṃbodhi* (三菩提) and perfect the light of all-knowing wisdom.' Having heard these words, I came to pay my respects. What I lament is my decrepitude, that I shall not encounter his holy transformation." At the south gate of the city, there is a stūpa; this is the place where the prince competed in strength with the other Śākyas and threw an elephant. The prince was highly skilled in many arts, standing alone and peerless. King Śuddhodana, feeling joy, was about to return when a servant was driving an elephant, just as they were about to exit the city. Devadatta, who had long prided himself on his great strength, was entering from outside and asked the driver, "You have prepared this elephant; who is to ride it?" He replied, "The prince is about to return, so I am going to serve as his driver." Devadatta, in a fit of anger, pulled the elephant, struck its forehead, and kicked its chest, causing it to fall dead and block the road, obstructing the path so that it could not be moved, and the crowd became congested. Nanda arrived later and asked, "Who killed this elephant?" They replied, "Devadatta." He immediately dragged it aside to clear the path. When the prince arrived, he also asked, "Who committed this evil act and killed this elephant?" They replied, "Devadatta killed it to block the gate, and Nanda dragged it away to open the path." The prince then lifted the elephant and flung it high, over the city moat. Where the elephant fell to the ground, it formed a large, deep pit, which local tradition calls the Pit of the Fallen Elephant. In a vihāra (精舍) beside it, a statue of the prince has been made. Beside that is another vihāra, which was the bedchamber of the prince's consort; inside are statues of Yaśodharā and Rāhula. In the vihāra beside the palace, a statue has been made in the posture of receiving instruction; this is the original site of the prince’s schoolroom. At the southeast corner of the city is a vihāra containing a statue of the prince riding a white horse through the air, marking the spot where he leaped over the city wall. Outside each of the four city gates is a vihāra containing statues of an old man, a sick man, a dead man, and a *śramaṇa*. These represent the prince’s excursions, where, upon seeing these signs, his anxiety increased and he became deeply weary of the mundane world; it was here that he was awakened [to renunciation] and ordered his servant to turn the carriage back.

zh: 城南行五十餘里，至故城，有窣堵波，是賢劫中人壽六萬歲時，迦羅迦村馱佛本生城也。城南不遠有窣堵波，成正覺已見父之處。城東南窣堵波，有彼如來遺身舍利。前建石柱，高三十餘尺，上刻師子之像，傍記寂滅之事，無憂王建焉。
en_current: Traveling over fifty *li* south of the city, one reaches an ancient city containing a *stūpa*; this was the birthplace of the Buddha Krakucchanda (迦羅迦村馱佛) during the Bhadrakalpa, when the human lifespan was sixty thousand years. Not far to the south of the city is a *stūpa* marking the place where he met his father after attaining full enlightenment. To the southeast of the city is a *stūpa* containing the relics of that Tathāgata’s remains. In front of it stands a stone pillar over thirty feet high, on top of which is carved the image of a lion, with an inscription on the side recording the events of his *parinirvāṇa*; it was erected by King Aśoka (無憂王).

zh: 迦羅迦村馱佛城東北行三十餘里，至故大城，中有窣堵波，是賢劫中人壽四萬歲時，迦諾迦牟尼佛本生城也。東北不遠有窣堵波，成正覺已度父之處。次北窣堵波，有彼如來遺身舍利，前建石柱，高二十餘尺，上刻師子之像，傍記寂滅之事，無憂王建也。
en_current: Traveling more than thirty li northeast from the city of Krakucchanda Buddha (迦羅迦村馱佛), one reaches an ancient great city. Inside it is a stupa; this is the native city of Kanakamuni Buddha (迦諾迦牟尼佛) from the time in the Bhadrakalpa when the human lifespan was forty thousand years. Not far to the northeast is a stupa, which is the place where, having attained perfect enlightenment, he converted his father. To the north of this is a stupa containing the relics of that Tathagata’s physical body. In front of it stands a stone pillar over twenty feet high, with the image of a lion carved on top and an account of his nirvana inscribed on the side, erected by King Aśoka (無憂王).

zh: 城東北四十餘里，有窣堵波，是太子坐樹陰，觀耕田，於此習定，而得離欲。淨飯王見太子坐樹陰，入寂定，日光逈照，樹影不移，心知靈聖，更深珍敬。大城西北，有數百千窣堵波，釋種誅死處也。毘盧釋迦王既克諸釋，虜其族類，得九千九百九十萬人，並從殺戮，積尸如莾，流血成池。天警人心，收骸瘞葬。誅釋西南，有四小窣堵波，四釋種拒軍處。初，勝軍王嗣位也，求婚釋種。釋種鄙其非類，謬以家人之女，重禮娉焉。勝軍王立為正后，其產子男，是為毘盧釋迦王。毘盧釋迦欲就舅氏請益受業，至此城南，見新講堂，即中憩駕。諸釋聞之，逐而詈曰：「卑賤婢子，敢居此室！此室諸釋建也，擬佛居焉。」毘盧釋迦嗣位之後，追復先辱，便興甲兵，至此屯軍。釋種四人躬耕畎畝，便即抗拒，兵寇退散，已而入城。族人以為承輪王之祚胤，為法王之宗子，敢行凶暴，安忍殺害，污辱宗門，絕親遠放。四人被逐，北趣雪山，一為烏仗那國王，一為梵衍那國王，一為呬摩呾羅國王，一為商彌國王，奕世傳業，苗裔不絕。
en_current: More than forty li to the northeast of the city, there is a stūpa marking the place where the Prince sat in the shade of a tree, watched the plowing of the fields, and practiced meditation, thereby attaining freedom from desire. When King Śuddhodana (淨飯王) saw the Prince sitting in the shade of the tree, having entered into tranquil meditation, while the sunlight shone brightly yet the shadow of the tree did not move, he knew in his heart that the Prince was spiritually holy, and he cherished and respected him all the more.  To the northwest of the great city, there are several hundred thousand stūpas; these are the places where the Śākya clan were slaughtered. After King Virūḍhaka (毘盧釋迦王) had conquered the Śākyas, he took their kin captive, obtaining ninety-nine million nine hundred thousand people, all of whom he put to death. The piled-up corpses were like a thicket, and the flowing blood formed a pond. Heaven stirred the hearts of men, and they gathered the remains and buried them.  To the southwest of the place where the Śākyas were slaughtered, there are four small stūpas; these are the places where four Śākya men resisted the army. Originally, when King Prasenajit (勝軍王) ascended the throne, he sought a marriage alliance with the Śākyas. The Śākyas, despising him as not being of their own kind, deceitfully gave him the daughter of a servant, yet they betrothed her with great ceremony. King Prasenajit established her as his principal queen, and she gave birth to a son, who was King Virūḍhaka.  When Virūḍhaka wished to go to his maternal uncles to request instruction and pursue his studies, he arrived south of this city and, seeing a new lecture hall, stopped his carriage to rest inside. When the Śākyas heard of this, they drove him out, cursing him: "You base-born slave, how dare you occupy this hall! This hall was built by the Śākyas, intended for the Buddha to reside in." After Virūḍhaka ascended the throne, he sought to avenge this former humiliation, so he raised an army and marched to this place to encamp his troops. Four members of the Śākya clan, who were personally plowing the fields, immediately resisted them; the invading army retreated and dispersed, and the four men then entered the city. Their clansmen, believing that as descendants of a Universal Monarch (cakravartin) and sons of the Dharma King, they should not have dared to commit acts of violence or heartlessly kill others, felt they had disgraced the clan; consequently, they severed ties with them and sent them into distant exile. After the four men were expelled, they fled north to the Snow Mountains; one became the king of Uḍḍiyāna (烏仗那國), one the king of Bāmīyān (梵衍那國), one the king of Himatala (呬摩呾羅國), and one the king of Śami (商彌國). Their dynasties passed down the throne for generations, and their lineage remained unbroken.

name_zh: 尼拘律樹林 (尼拘盧陀僧伽藍)
zh: 城南三四里尼拘律樹林，有窣堵波，無憂王建也。釋迦如來成正覺已，還國見父王，為說法處。淨飯王知如來降魔軍已，遊行化導，情懷渴仰，思得禮敬。乃命使請如來曰：「昔期成佛，當還本生。斯言在耳，時來降趾。」使至佛所，具宣王意。如來告曰：「却後七日，當還本生。」使臣還以白王，淨飯王乃告命臣庶，灑掃衢路，儲積華香，與諸群臣四十里外佇駕奉迎。是時如來與大眾俱，八金剛周衛，四天王前導，帝釋與欲界天侍左，梵王與色界天侍右，諸苾芻僧列在其後。維佛在眾，如月映星，威神動三界，光明踰七曜，步虛空，至生國。王與從臣禮敬已畢，俱共還國，止尼拘盧陀僧伽藍。其側不遠有窣堵波，是如來於大樹下，東面而坐，受姨母金縷袈裟。次此窣堵波，是如來於此度八王子及五百釋種。城東門內路左，有窣堵波，昔一切義成太子於此習諸技藝。門外有自在天祠，祠中石天像，危然起勢，是太子在襁褓中所入祠也。淨飯王自臘伐尼國迎太子還也，途次天祠。王曰：「此天祠多靈鑒，諸釋童稚求祐必効，宜將太子至彼修敬。」是時傅母抱而入祠，其石天像起迎太子。太子已出，天像復坐。城南門外路左，有窣堵波，是太子與諸釋角藝，射鐵鼓。
en_current: Three or four li to the south of the city is a Nyagrodha (尼拘律) forest, where there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王). This is the place where the Śākya Tathāgata, having attained perfect enlightenment, returned to his home country to see his royal father and preach the Dharma. When King Śuddhodana (淨飯王) learned that the Tathāgata had already subdued the army of Māra and was traveling about to teach and guide others, his heart was filled with longing and he wished to pay his respects. He then commanded a messenger to invite the Tathāgata, saying: "Formerly you promised that upon attaining Buddhahood, you would return to your place of birth. These words are still in my ears; the time has come for you to arrive." The messenger reached the Buddha and fully conveyed the king's intent. The Tathāgata replied: "Seven days from now, I shall return to my place of birth." The messenger returned and reported this to the king. King Śuddhodana then ordered his officials and subjects to sprinkle and sweep the roads and to gather flowers and incense, and he went out forty li with his ministers to wait for the carriage and welcome him.  At that time, the Tathāgata was with the great assembly, surrounded by the eight Vajra-warriors, led by the Four Heavenly Kings, with Indra (帝釋) and the devas of the Desire Realm attending on the left, Brahmā (梵王) and the devas of the Form Realm attending on the right, and the congregation of bhikṣus following behind. As the Buddha stood among the assembly, he was like the moon reflecting among the stars; his majestic power moved the three realms, and his radiance surpassed the seven luminaries as he walked through the void to reach his birth country. After the king and his ministers had finished paying their respects, they all returned to the city together and stayed at the Nyagrodha (尼拘盧陀) monastery. Not far to the side of this is a stūpa, which is where the Tathāgata sat facing east under a large tree and accepted the golden-threaded monastic robe from his aunt. Next to this stūpa is another, where the Tathāgata converted the eight princes and five hundred members of the Śākya clan. Inside the east gate of the city, on the left side of the road, there is a stūpa where, in the past, the Bodhisattva Prince Sarvārthasiddha (一切義成) practiced various arts. Outside the gate is a temple of Īśvara (自在天); inside the temple is a stone image of the deity in a towering, rising posture, which is the temple the Prince entered while still in his swaddling clothes. When King Śuddhodana (淨飯王) was escorting the Prince back from the country of Lumbinī (臘伐尼國), they passed by this celestial temple on their way. The King said, "This temple is known for its many spiritual manifestations; whenever the children of the Śākya clan seek protection here, their prayers are always answered; we should take the Prince there to pay his respects." At that time, the wet nurse carried the Prince into the temple, and the stone image of the deity rose to greet the Prince. Once the Prince had left, the image returned to its seated position. Outside the south gate of the city, on the left side of the road, there is a stūpa where the Prince competed in arts with the other Śākyas and shot through iron drums.

zh: 從此東南三十餘里，有小窣堵波，其側有泉，泉流澄鏡，是太子與諸釋引強校能，弦矢既分，穿鼓過表，至池沒羽，因涌清流，時俗相傳，謂之箭泉。夫有疾病，飲沐多愈。遠方之人持泥以歸，隨其所苦，漬以塗額，靈神冥衛，多蒙痊愈。
en_current: More than thirty *li* to the southeast from here is a small *stūpa*. Beside it is a spring with water as clear as a mirror. This is where the prince competed in strength and skill with the other Śākyas; when the arrow left the string, it pierced the drums, passed through the target, and buried its feathers in the pool, causing a clear stream to gush forth. Popular tradition calls it the Arrow Spring (Śarakūpa). Those who suffer from illnesses are often cured by drinking from it or bathing in it. People from distant lands take the mud home and, according to their afflictions, moisten it to apply to their foreheads; through the secret protection of the divine spirits, most of them are healed.

zh: 箭泉東北行八九十里，至臘伐尼林，有釋種浴池，澄清皎鏡，雜華彌漫。其北二十四五步，有無憂華樹，今已枯悴，菩薩誕靈之處。菩薩以吠舍佉月後半八日，當此三月八日；上座部則曰以吠舍佉月後半十五日，當此三月十五日。次東窣堵波，無憂王所建，二龍浴太子處也。菩薩生已，不扶而行，於四方各七步，而自言曰：「天上、天下，唯我獨尊。今茲而往，生分已盡。」隨足所蹈，出大蓮花。二龍踊出，住虛空中，而各吐水，一冷一煖，以浴太子。浴太子窣堵波東，有二清泉，傍建二窣堵波，是二龍從地踊出之處。菩薩生已，支屬宗親莫不奔馳，求水盥浴。夫人之前，二泉涌出，一冷一煖，遂以浴洗。其南窣堵波，是天帝釋捧接菩薩處。菩薩初出胎也，天帝釋以妙天衣，跪接菩薩。次有四窣堵波，是四天王抱持菩薩處也。菩薩從右脇生已，四大天王以金色㲲衣，捧菩薩，置金机上。至母前曰：「夫人誕斯福子，誠可歡慶。諸天尚喜，況世人乎？」
en_current: Traveling eighty or ninety *li* northeast from the Arrow Spring (Śarakūpa), one arrives at the Lumbinī Grove (臘伐尼林). There is a bathing pool of the Śākya clan, clear and bright as a mirror, with various flowers blooming in profusion. Twenty-four or twenty-five paces to its north is an Aśoka tree (無憂華樹), now withered and dry, which is the place where the Bodhisattva was born. The Bodhisattva was born on the eighth day of the second half of the month of Vaiśākha, which corresponds to the eighth day of the third month; the Sthavira school, however, says it was on the fifteenth day of the second half of the month of Vaiśākha, which corresponds to the fifteenth day of the third month. To the east is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王), the place where the two dragons bathed the prince. After the Bodhisattva was born, he walked seven paces in each of the four directions without assistance and declared, "In the heavens above and on earth below, I alone am the honored one. From this time forward, the cycle of birth is at an end." Wherever his feet stepped, a large lotus flower emerged. Two dragons leaped forth and remained in the void, each spitting out water—one cold and one warm—to bathe the prince. To the east of the stūpa marking the bathing of the prince are two clear springs, beside which two stūpas were built at the spot where the two dragons emerged from the earth. After the Bodhisattva was born, his relatives and kin all rushed about, seeking water for washing and bathing. In front of the Lady, two springs gushed forth, one cold and one warm, which were then used for the bathing. The stūpa to the south is the place where Śakra Devendra (天帝釋) received the Bodhisattva. When the Bodhisattva first emerged from the womb, Śakra Devendra knelt and received the Bodhisattva with a wondrous heavenly garment. Next are four stūpas, which are the places where the Four Heavenly Kings (Caturmahārāja) held the Bodhisattva. After the Bodhisattva was born from the right side, the Four Great Heavenly Kings received the Bodhisattva with a golden-colored fine cotton cloth and placed him on a golden table. They approached the Lady and said, "The Lady has given birth to this blessed child; it is truly a cause for rejoicing. Even the gods are joyful, how much more so should the people of the world be?"

name_zh: 臘伐尼林無憂王石柱・油河
zh: 四天王捧太子窣堵波側不遠，有大石柱，上作馬像，無憂王之所建也。後為惡龍霹靂，其柱中折仆地。傍有小河，東南流，土俗號曰油河。是摩耶夫人產孕已，天化此池，光潤澄淨，欲令夫人取以沐浴，除去風虛。今變為水，其流尚膩。
en_current: Not far from the side of the stupa where the Four Heavenly Kings (Caturmahārāja) held the prince, there is a great stone pillar with the figure of a horse on top, which was erected by King Ashoka (Aśoka). Later, due to a thunderbolt caused by an evil dragon, the pillar was broken in the middle and fell to the ground. Beside it is a small river flowing southeast, which the local people call the Oil River. After Queen Māyā (Māyādevī) had given birth, the gods manifested this pond, its water glossy and pure, intending for the Queen to bathe in it to remove the wind-related infirmities. It has now changed into water, yet its current remains greasy.

zh: 宮城之側有一伽藍，僧徒三千餘人，習學小乘正量部教。
en_current: Beside the palace city is a monastery with more than three thousand monks, who study the teachings of the Saṃmitīya school (正量部) of the Hīnayāna.

name_zh: 淨飯王正殿・摩耶夫人寢殿
zh: 宮城內有故基，淨飯王正殿也。上建精舍，中作王像。其側不遠有故基，摩訶摩耶（唐言大術）夫人寢殿也。上建精舍，中作夫人之像。其側精舍，是釋迦菩薩降神母胎處，中作菩薩降神之像。
en_current: Within the palace city are old foundations, which are the main hall of King Śuddhodana (淨飯王). A *vihāra* (精舍) has been built upon it, inside of which is a statue of the king. Not far to the side are old foundations, which are the bedchamber of Queen Mahāmāyā (摩訶摩耶; Tang language: Great Illusion) (大術). A *vihāra* has been built upon it, inside of which is a statue of the queen. The *vihāra* to the side is the place where the Bodhisattva Śākya descended into his mother’s womb, and inside is a representation of the Bodhisattva’s descent.

zh: 菩薩降神東北，有窣堵波，阿私多仙相太子處。菩薩誕靈之日，嘉祥輻湊。時淨飯王召諸相師而告之曰：「此子生也，善惡何若？宜悉乃正，明言以對。」曰：「依先聖之記，考吉祥之應，在家作轉輪聖王，捨家當成等正覺。」是時阿私多仙自遠而至，叩門請見。王甚慶悅，躬迎禮敬，請就寶座，曰：「不意大仙今日降顧。」仙曰：「我在天宮安居宴坐，忽見諸天群從蹈舞，我時問言：『何悅豫之甚也？』曰：『大仙當知，贍部洲中釋種淨飯王第一夫人，今產太子，當證三菩提，圓明一切智。』我聞是語，故來瞻仰。所悲朽耄，不遭聖化。」
en_current: To the northeast of the place where the Bodhisattva’s spirit descended, there is a stūpa at the site where the rishi Asita (阿私多) read the prince’s physiognomy. On the day the Bodhisattva was born, auspicious signs converged. At that time, King Śuddhodana (淨飯王) summoned the various physiognomists and said to them: "This child has been born; what is his fortune, good or evil? You must examine him thoroughly and speak clearly in your reply." They said: "According to the records of the ancient sages and examining the auspicious omens, if he remains in household life, he will become a Cakravartin (轉輪聖王); if he renounces the household, he will surely attain Samyak-saṃbodhi (等正覺)." At that time, the rishi Asita came from afar and knocked at the gate, requesting an audience. The king was greatly delighted; he personally welcomed him with respect, invited him to a precious seat, and said: "I did not expect that you, Great Seer, would condescend to visit today." The seer said: "While I was dwelling in peace and sitting at ease in the heavenly palace, I suddenly saw hosts of devas dancing. I then asked them, 'Why are you so extremely joyful?' They replied, 'Great Seer, you should know that the first lady of King Śuddhodana of the Śākya clan in Jambudvīpa (贍部洲) has now given birth to a prince, who shall realize *saṃbodhi* (三菩提) and perfectly illuminate all-encompassing wisdom.' Having heard these words, I have come to pay my respects. What I grieve is that I am old and decrepit, and will not encounter his holy transformation."

name_zh: 角力擲象窣堵波・象墮阬
zh: 城南門有窣堵波，是太子與諸釋角力擲象之處。太子伎藝多能，獨拔倫匹。淨飯大王懷慶將返，僕夫馭象，方欲出城。提婆達多素負強力，自外而入，問馭者曰：「嚴駕此象，其誰欲乘？」曰：「太子將還，故往奉馭。」提婆達多發憤引象，批其顙，蹴其臆，僵仆塞路，杜絕行途，無能轉移，人眾填塞。難陀後至，而問之曰：「誰死此象？」曰：「提婆達多。」即曳之避路。太子至，又問曰：「誰為不善，害此象耶？」曰：「提婆達多害以杜門，難陀引之開徑。」太子乃舉象高擲，越度城塹，其象墮地，為大深阬，土俗相傳為象墮阬也。
en_current: At the south gate of the city there is a stūpa, which is the place where the prince and the various Śākyas competed in feats of strength and threw the elephant. The prince was highly skilled in many arts, standing alone and peerless. King Śuddhodana (淨飯大王), feeling joyful, was about to return, and a servant was driving an elephant, just intending to exit the city. Devadatta (提婆達多), who had always prided himself on his great strength, came in from outside and asked the driver, "For whom has this elephant been so grandly harnessed, and who intends to ride it?" He replied, "The prince is about to return, so I am going to serve him." Devadatta, in a fit of rage, seized the elephant, struck it on the forehead, and kicked it in the chest, causing it to fall dead and block the road; it obstructed the way so that no one could move it, and a great crowd gathered. Nanda (難陀) arrived later and asked, "Who killed this elephant?" They replied, "Devadatta." He then dragged it aside to clear the road. When the prince arrived, he also asked, "Who has done this evil deed and killed this elephant?" They replied, "Devadatta killed it to block the gate, and Nanda dragged it to open the path." The prince then lifted the elephant and flung it high across the city moat; where the elephant fell to the ground, it formed a large, deep pit, which local tradition calls the Pit of the Fallen Elephant.

zh: 其側又有精舍，太子妃寢宮也，中作耶輸陀羅，并有羅怙羅像。
en_current: Beside it is another *vihāra* (精舍), which was the bedchamber of the prince’s consort; inside are images of Yaśodharā and Rāhula.

zh: 宮側精舍作受業之像，太子學堂故基也。
en_current: Beside the palace is a *vihāra* (精舍) containing a statue in the posture of receiving instruction; this is the former site of the prince’s schoolroom.

zh: 城東南隅有一精舍，中作太子乘白馬凌虛之像，是踰城處也。
en_current: At the southeast corner of the city is a *vihāra* (精舍), inside which is fashioned an image of the prince riding a white horse through the void; this is the place where he leaped over the city wall.

zh: 城四門外各有精舍，中作老、病、死人、沙門之像。是太子遊觀，覩相增懷，深厭塵俗，於此感悟，命僕迴駕。
en_current: Outside each of the four city gates there is a *vihāra* (精舍), in which are fashioned images of an old man, a sick man, a dead man, and a śramaṇa. These mark the places where the prince, while out on an excursion, observed these sights and grew pensive, feeling a deep aversion to worldly life; having attained this realization, he ordered his servant to turn the carriage back.

zh: 大城西北，有數百千窣堵波，釋種誅死處也。毘盧釋迦王既克諸釋，虜其族類，得九千九百九十萬人，並從殺戮，積尸如莾，流血成池。天警人心，收骸瘞葬。
en_current: To the northwest of the great city, there are hundreds of thousands of stūpas, which is the place where the Śākya clan (釋種) was slaughtered. After King Virūḍhaka (毘盧釋迦王) had conquered the Śākyas, he captured their tribesmen, obtaining ninety-nine million nine hundred thousand people, and massacred them all; the corpses were piled up like thickets, and the flowing blood formed a pool. Heaven moved the hearts of men to collect the remains and bury them.

zh: 門外有自在天祠，祠中石天像，危然起勢，是太子在襁褓中所入祠也。淨飯王自臘伐尼國迎太子還也，途次天祠。王曰：「此天祠多靈鑒，諸釋童稚求祐必効，宜將太子至彼修敬。」是時傅母抱而入祠，其石天像起迎太子。太子已出，天像復坐。
en_current: Outside the gate is a temple of Maheśvara (自在天), in which there is a stone image of the deity in a towering, rising posture; this is the temple the Prince entered while still in his swaddling clothes. When King Śuddhodana (淨飯王) was escorting the Prince back from the country of Lumbinī (臘伐尼國), they passed by this celestial temple on their way. The King said, "This temple is known for its many spiritual manifestations; whenever the children of the Śākya (釋) clan seek protection here, their prayers are always answered; we should take the Prince there to pay his respects." At that time, the wet nurse carried the Prince into the temple, and the stone image of the deity rose to greet him. Once the Prince had left, the image of the deity sat down again.

zh: 城南門外路左，有窣堵波，是太子與諸釋角藝，射鐵鼓。
en_current: Outside the south gate of the city, on the left side of the road, there is a stūpa (窣堵波) where the Prince competed in arts with the various Śākyas and shot through the iron drums.

zh: 從此東行曠野荒林中二百餘里，至藍摩國（中印度境）。藍摩國，空荒歲久，疆埸無紀，城邑丘墟，居人稀曠。故城東南有甎窣堵波，高減百尺。昔者如來入寂滅已，此國先王分得舍利，持歸本國，式遵崇建，靈異間起，神光時燭。窣堵波側有一清池，龍每出遊，變形蛇服，右旋宛轉，繞窣堵波，野象群行，採花以散，冥力警察，初無間替。昔無憂王之分建窣堵波也，七國所建，咸已開發，至於此國，方欲興功，而此池龍恐見陵奪，乃變作婆羅門，前叩象曰：「大王情流佛法，廣樹福田，敢請紆駕，降臨我宅。」王曰：「爾家安在，為近遠乎？」婆羅門曰：「我，此池之龍王也。承大王欲建勝福，敢來請謁。」王受其請，遂入龍宮。坐久之，龍進曰：「我惟惡業，受此龍身，供養舍利，冀消罪咎，願王躬往，觀而禮敬。」無憂王見已，懼然謂曰：「凡諸供養之具，非人間所有也。」龍曰：「若然者，願無廢毀。」無憂王自度力非其疇，遂不開發。出池之所，今有封記。窣堵波側不遠，有一伽藍，僧眾尠矣，清肅皎然，而以沙彌總任眾務。遠方僧至，禮遇彌隆，必留三日，供養四事。聞諸先志曰：昔有苾芻，同志相召，自遠而至，禮窣堵波。見諸群象，相趨往來，或以牙芟草，或以鼻灑水，各持異華，共為供養。時眾見已，悲歎感懷。有一苾芻，便捨具戒，願留供養，與眾辭曰：「我惟多福，濫迹僧中，歲月亟淹，行業無紀。此窣堵波有佛舍利，聖德冥通，群象踐灑。遺身此地，甘與同群，得畢餘齡，誠為幸矣。」眾告之曰：「斯盛事也。吾等垢重，智不謀此。隨時自愛，無虧勝業。」亦既離群，重申誠願，歡然獨居，有終焉之志。於是葺茅為宇，引流成池，採掇時花，灑掃塋域。綿歷歲序，心事無殆。隣國諸王聞而雅尚，競捨財寶，共建伽藍，因而勸請，屈知僧務。自爾相踵，不泯元功，而以沙彌總知僧事。
en_current: From here, traveling east through a wilderness and desolate forest for more than two hundred *li*, one arrives at the country of Rāmagrāma (藍摩國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Rāmagrāma has been desolate for a long time; its borders are undefined, its cities and towns are in ruins, and its inhabitants are few and scattered. To the southeast of the old city, there is a brick *stūpa* slightly less than one hundred feet high. Formerly, after the Tathāgata entered *parinirvāṇa*, the former king of this country obtained a share of the relics, brought them back to his own country, and duly honored them by building [this structure]. Miraculous signs appeared from time to time, and divine light shone occasionally. Beside the *stūpa* is a clear pool; the dragon often emerges to wander, changing its form into that of a snake, circling the *stūpa* to the right in winding movements. Herds of wild elephants come to gather flowers and scatter them [as offerings]; this spiritual influence keeps watch, and there has never been any interruption. Formerly, when King Aśoka (無憂王) was distributing [relics] to build *stūpas*, those built by the seven [other] kingdoms had all been opened. When he arrived in this country and was about to begin the work, the dragon of this pool, fearing they would be seized and taken away, transformed into a Brahmin, approached the elephant, and said: "Your Majesty’s devotion flows toward the Buddha-dharma, and you have widely planted fields of merit; I venture to ask you to deign to visit my abode." The King said: "Where is your home? Is it near or far?" The Brahmin said: "I am the Dragon King of this pool. Having heard that Your Majesty wishes to build superior merit, I have ventured to come and invite you." The King accepted his invitation and thereupon entered the dragon palace. After sitting for a long time, the dragon approached and said: "Because of my evil karma, I have received this dragon body. I make offerings to the relics, hoping to eliminate my sins and faults. I wish for the King to go in person to observe and pay homage." When King Aśoka (無憂王) saw them, he said with trepidation: "All these implements of offering are not things of the human world." The dragon said: "If that is so, I hope you will not destroy or damage them." King Aśoka judged that his own power was not a match for theirs, and so he did not open them. The place where he emerged from the pool now has a marker.  Not far from the side of the stupa (窣堵波) is a monastery (伽藍); the community of monks is small, and the place is pure, solemn, and bright, with a novice (沙彌) in charge of all the affairs of the community. When monks from afar arrive, they are treated with great respect; they are always kept for three days and provided with the four requisites.  According to ancient records, there were once bhikṣus who, having invited one another, came from afar to pay homage at the stupa. They saw herds of elephants coming and going; some used their tusks to clear away grass, others used their trunks to sprinkle water, and each held different flowers to make offerings together. When the group saw this, they were moved to sadness and reflection. One bhikṣu then renounced his full precepts, wishing to remain and make offerings. He said to the group: "I have had much good fortune, but I have merely left traces among the sangha; years and months have passed quickly, yet my practice has no record. This stupa contains the Buddha’s relics, and his holy virtue reaches into the unseen, causing herds of elephants to tread and sprinkle it. To leave my body in this place and be willing to join this group, to be able to finish the remainder of my life here, would truly be a blessing." The group said to him: "This is a magnificent undertaking. We are heavy with defilements, and our wisdom does not reach this far. Take good care of yourself at all times, and do not fall short in this excellent work." Having parted from the group, he reaffirmed his sincere vow, lived alone in joy, and held the determination to remain there until the end of his days. He then thatched a hut for a dwelling, diverted a stream to form a pond, gathered seasonal flowers, and sprinkled and swept the burial area. As the years and months passed, his devotion never faltered. The kings of neighboring countries heard of this and held him in high esteem; they vied with one another to donate treasures to jointly build a monastery, and subsequently invited him to deign to oversee the monastic affairs. Since then, this tradition has been followed in succession so as not to let his original merit be forgotten, and a śrāmaṇera (沙彌) is always appointed to manage the affairs of the monastery.

name_zh: 太子迴駕・剃髮窣堵波
zh: 沙彌伽藍東，大林中行百餘里，至大窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。是太子踰城至此，解寶衣，去纓絡，命僕還處。太子夜半踰城，遲明至此，既允宿心，乃形言曰：「是我出籠樊，去羈鎖，最後釋駕之處也。」於天冠中解末尼寶，命僕夫曰：「汝持此寶，還白父王，今茲遠遁，非苟違離，欲斷無常，絕諸有漏。」闡鐸迦（舊曰車匿，訛也）曰：「詎有何心，空駕而返？」太子善言慰喻，感悟而還。迴駕窣堵波東，有贍部樹，枝葉雖凋，枯株尚在。其傍復有小窣堵波，太子以餘寶衣易鹿皮衣處。太子既斷髮易裳，雖去瓔珞，尚有天衣。曰：「斯服太侈，如何改易？」時淨居天化作獵人，服鹿皮衣，持弓負羽。太子舉其衣而謂曰：「欲相貿易，願見允從。」獵人曰：「善。」太子解其上服，授與獵人。獵人得已，還復天身，持所得衣，凌虛而去。太子易衣側不遠，有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也，是太子剃髮處。太子從闡鐸迦取刀，自斷其髮，天帝釋接上天宮，以為供養。時淨居天子化作剃髮人，執持銛刀，徐步而至。太子謂曰：「能剃髮乎？幸為我淨之。」化人受命，遂為剃髮。踰城出家時亦不定，或云菩薩年十九，或曰二十九，以吠舍佉月後半八日踰城出家，當此三月八日，或云以吠舍佉月後半十五日，當此三月十五日。
en_current: To the east of the Śrāmaṇera Monastery, traveling more than one hundred *li* through a great forest, one reaches a large stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王). This is the place where the Prince, having scaled the city walls and arrived here, took off his precious garments, removed his necklaces, and ordered his servant to return. The Prince had scaled the city walls at midnight and reached this place at dawn; having fulfilled his long-cherished wish, he spoke aloud, saying: "This is the place where I escape the cage, cast off the fetters, and finally unyoke my carriage." He took the *maṇi* jewel from his celestial crown and commanded his servant, saying: "Take this jewel and return to report to my father the King. My fleeing to this distant place is not out of a desire to abandon him, but to put an end to impermanence and sever all outflows." Chandaka (闡鐸迦) (The old term was Che-ni [車匿], which is incorrect) said: "How could I have the heart to return with an empty carriage?" The Prince comforted him with kind words, and he was moved to understanding and returned.  To the east of the "Returning Carriage" (迴駕) stūpa, there is a Jambu tree; although its branches and leaves have withered, the dead trunk still remains. Beside it is another small stūpa, marking the place where the Prince exchanged his remaining precious garments for a deerskin robe. After the Prince had cut his hair and changed his attire, although he had removed his necklaces, he still wore a celestial robe. He said: "This garment is too extravagant; how can I change it?" At that time, a Pure Abode Heaven (Śuddhāvāsa-deva) transformed into a hunter wearing a deerskin robe, carrying a bow and bearing feathers. The Prince raised his own garment and said to him: "I wish to trade with you; I hope you will consent." The hunter said: "Very well." The Prince took off his upper garment and handed it to the hunter. The hunter, having obtained it, resumed his celestial form, took the garment he had received, and ascended into the void to depart. Not far from where the Prince changed his clothes is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王), which is the place where the Prince shaved his hair. The Prince took a blade from Chandaka (闡鐸迦) and cut off his own hair; Śakra Devānām Indra (天帝釋) caught it and took it to the heavenly palace to be venerated. At that time, a son of the Pure Abode Heaven (Śuddhāvāsa-deva) transformed into a barber, holding a sharp blade, and approached with slow steps. The Prince said to him, "Can you shave my hair? I would be grateful if you would clean it for me." The transformed being accepted the command and proceeded to shave his hair. The time when he climbed over the city wall to renounce the household life is also uncertain; some say the Bodhisattva was nineteen years old, while others say he was twenty-nine. He climbed over the city wall to renounce the household life on the eighth day of the latter half of the month of Vaiśākha, which corresponds to the eighth day of the third month; others say it was on the fifteenth day of the latter half of the month of Vaiśākha, which corresponds to the fifteenth day of the third month.

name_zh: 尼拘盧陀林灰炭窣堵波
zh: 太子剃髮窣堵波東南，曠野中行百八九十里，至尼拘盧陀林，有窣堵波，高三十餘尺。昔如來寂滅，舍利已分，諸婆羅門無所得獲，於涅疊般那（唐言焚燒。舊云闍維，訛也）地收餘灰炭，持至本國，建此靈基，而修供養。自茲已降，奇迹相仍，疾病之人，祈請多愈。灰炭窣堵波側，故伽藍中，有過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。故伽藍左右，數百窣堵波。其一大者，無憂王所建也，崇基雖陷，高餘百尺。自此東北，大林中行，其路艱險，經途危阻，山牛、野象、群盜、獵師，伺求行旅，為害不絕。
en_current: Southeast from the stupa where the prince had his hair shaved, traveling one hundred and eighty or ninety li through a wilderness, one reaches the Nyagrodha grove (尼拘盧陀林), where there is a stupa over thirty feet high. In the past, when the Tathāgata attained parinirvāṇa and the relics had already been divided, the various Brahmins who had obtained none gathered the remaining ashes and charcoal at the place of the *niedie banna* (In Tang language this means cremation. The old term *shewei* is incorrect) and brought them to their own country, where they built this sacred foundation and performed offerings. From that time onward, miraculous signs have occurred in succession, and sick people who pray there are often healed. Beside the Ash Stupa, within an old monastery, there are sites where the four past Buddhas sat and performed walking meditation. Around this old monastery are several hundred stupas. One of them, which is large, was built by King Aśoka (無憂王); although its lofty base has collapsed, it is over one hundred feet high. From here, traveling northeast through a great forest, the road is difficult and dangerous; the route is perilous and obstructed, and wild oxen, wild elephants, bands of robbers, and hunters lie in wait for travelers, causing ceaseless harm.

zh: 出此林已，至拘尸那揭羅國（中印度境）。拘尸那揭羅國，城郭頹毀，邑里蕭條。故城甎基，周十餘里。居人稀曠，閭巷荒蕪。城內東北隅，有窣堵波，無憂王所建，准陀（舊曰純陀，訛也）之故宅也。宅中有井，將營獻供，方乃鑿焉。歲月雖淹，水猶清美。
en_current: After emerging from this forest, I reached the country of Kuśinagara (拘尸那揭羅國) (within the borders of Central India). In the country of Kuśinagara, the city walls are dilapidated and the towns and villages are desolate. The brick foundations of the old city measure more than ten li in circumference. The inhabitants are few and scattered, and the lanes and alleys are overgrown. In the northeast corner within the city, there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka on the site of the former residence of Cunda (准陀) (formerly called Chuntuo, which is a corruption). Inside the residence is a well; it was dug at the time he was preparing his offering. Although much time has passed, the water remains clear and sweet.

zh: 城西北三四里，渡阿恃多伐底河（唐言無勝，此世共稱耳。舊云阿利羅跋提河，訛也。典言謂之尸賴拏伐底河，譯曰有金河）。西岸不遠，至娑羅林。其樹類槲，而皮青白，葉甚光潤。四樹特高，如來寂滅之所也。其大甎精舍中作如來涅槃之像，北首而臥。傍有窣堵波，無憂王所建，基雖傾陷，尚高二百餘尺。前建石柱，以記如來寂滅之事，雖有文記，不書日月。聞諸先記曰：佛以生年八十，吠舍佉月後半十五日入般涅槃，當此三月十五日也。說一切有部則佛以迦剌底迦月後半八日入般涅槃，此當九月八日也。自佛涅槃，諸部異議，或云千二百餘年，或云千三百餘年，或云千五百餘年，或云已過九百，未滿千年。精舍側不遠，有窣堵波，是如來修菩薩行時，為群雉王救火之處。昔於此地有大茂林，毛群羽族巢居穴處。驚風四起，猛焰飈急。時有一雉，有懷傷愍，鼓濯清流，飛空奮灑。時天帝釋俯而告曰：「汝何守愚，虛勞羽翮？大火方起，焚燎林野，豈汝微軀所能撲滅？」雉曰：「說者為誰？」曰：「我天帝釋耳。」雉曰：「今天帝有大福力，無欲不遂，救災拯難，若指諸掌，反詰無功，其咎安在？猛火方熾，無得多言！」尋復奮飛，往趣流水。天帝遂以掬水泛灑其林，火滅煙消，生類全命，故今謂之救火窣堵波也。雉救火側不遠，有窣堵波，是如來修菩薩行時，為鹿救生之處。乃往古昔，此有大林，火炎中野，飛走窮窘，前有駛流之阨，後困猛火之難，莫不沈溺，喪棄身命。其鹿惻隱，身據橫流，穿皮斷骨，自強拯溺。蹇兔後至，忍疲苦而濟之。筋力既竭，溺水而死。諸天收骸，起窣堵波。鹿拯溺西不遠，有窣堵波，是蘇跋陀羅（唐言善賢。舊曰須跋陀羅，訛也）入寂滅之處。善賢者，本梵志師也。年百二十，耆舊多智。聞佛寂滅，至雙樹間，問阿難曰：「佛世尊將寂滅，我懷疑滯，願欲請問。」阿難曰：「佛將涅槃，幸無擾也。」曰：「吾聞佛世難遇，正法難聞，我有深疑，恐無所請。」善賢遂入，先問佛言：「有諸別眾，自稱為師，各有異法，垂訓導俗，喬答摩（舊曰瞿曇，訛略也）能盡知耶？」佛言：「吾悉深究。」乃為演說。善賢聞已，心淨信解，求入法中，受具足戒。如來告曰：「汝豈能耶？外道異學修梵行者，當試四歲，觀其行，察其性，威儀寂靜，辭語誠實，則可於我法中淨修梵行。在人行耳，斯何難哉！」善賢曰：「世尊悲愍，含濟無私，四歲試學，三業方順。」佛言：「我先已說，在人行耳！」於是善賢出家，即受具戒，勤勵修習，身心勇猛。已而於法無疑，自身作證。夜分未久，果證羅漢，諸漏已盡，梵行已立。不忍見佛入大涅槃，即於眾中入火界定，現神通事，而先寂滅。是為如來最後弟子，乃先滅度，即昔後渡蹇兔是也。善賢寂滅側，有窣堵波，是執金剛躄地之處。大悲世尊隨機利見，化功已畢，入寂滅樂，於雙樹間北首而臥。執金剛神密迹力士見佛滅度，悲慟唱言：「如來捨我入大涅槃，無歸依，無覆護，毒箭深入，愁火熾盛！」捨金剛杵，悶絕躄地。久而又起，悲哀戀慕，互相謂曰：「生死大海，誰作舟檝？無明長夜，誰為燈炬？」金剛躄地側，有窣堵波，是如來寂滅已七日供養之處。如來之將寂滅也，光明普照，人、天畢會，莫不悲感，更相謂曰：「大覺世尊今將寂滅，眾生福盡，世間無依。」如來右脇臥師子床，告諸大眾：「勿謂如來畢竟寂滅，法身常住，離諸變易，當棄懈怠，早求解脫。」諸苾芻等歔欷悲慟。時阿泥𢫫（盧骨反）陀（舊曰阿那律，訛也）告諸苾芻：「止，止，勿悲！諸天譏怪。」時末羅眾供養已訖，欲舉金棺，詣涅疊般那所。時阿泥𢫫陀告言：「且止！諸天欲留七日供養。」於是天眾持妙天華，遊虛空，讚聖德，各竭誠心，共興供養。停棺側有窣堵波，是摩訶摩耶夫人哭佛之處。如來寂滅，棺斂已畢，時阿泥𢫫陀上昇天宮，告摩耶夫人曰：「大聖法王今已寂滅。」摩耶聞已，悲哽悶絕，與諸天眾至雙樹間，見僧伽胝、鉢及錫杖，拊之號慟，絕而復聲曰：「人、天福盡，世間眼滅！今此諸物，空無有主。」如來聖力，金棺自開，放光明，合掌坐，慰問慈母：「遠來下降！諸行法爾，願勿深悲。」阿難銜哀而請佛曰：「後世問我，將何以對？」曰：「佛已涅槃，慈母摩耶自天宮降，至雙樹間，如來為諸不孝眾生，從金棺起，合掌說法。」
en_current: Three or four *li* to the northwest of the city, one crosses the Ajitavatī River (阿恃多伐底河) (in the Tang language, "Invincible"; this is merely the common name in this world. The old name, Alilobati River (阿利羅跋提河), is a corruption. The classical language calls it the Hiraṇyavatī River, which translates as "River of Gold"). Not far from the west bank, one reaches the Sāla (娑羅) grove. The trees resemble the oak, but their bark is greenish-white and their leaves are very glossy and smooth. Four trees are particularly tall; this is the place where the Tathāgata attained extinction (parinirvāṇa). In the large brick vihāra (精舍) is an image of the Tathāgata in the state of *nirvāṇa*, lying with his head to the north. Beside it is a *stūpa* built by King Aśoka; although the base has collapsed and sunken, it is still over two hundred feet high. In front of it stands a stone pillar recording the event of the Tathāgata’s extinction; although there is an inscription, it does not record the year or month. I have heard from ancient records that the Buddha entered *parinirvāṇa* at the age of eighty on the fifteenth day of the second half of the month of Vaiśākha, which corresponds to the fifteenth day of the third month. The Sarvāstivāda school, however, holds that the Buddha entered *parinirvāṇa* on the eighth day of the second half of the month of Kārttika, which corresponds to the eighth day of the ninth month. Since the Buddha’s *nirvāṇa*, the various schools have held differing opinions: some say more than 1,200 years have passed, some say more than 1,300 years, some say more than 1,500 years, and others say more than 900 but less than 1,000 years. Not far from the side of the vihāra is a *stūpa* marking the place where the Tathāgata, when practicing the Bodhisattva path, acted as the king of a flock of pheasants to save them from a fire. Formerly, there was a great, dense forest in this place, where feathered and furred creatures nested and lived in burrows. Sudden winds arose from all directions, and the fierce flames surged rapidly. At that time, there was a pheasant who, moved by compassion, soaked its wings in a clear stream and flew into the air to sprinkle the water. The Heavenly Emperor Śakra (天帝釋) looked down and said to it, "Why are you so foolish, exhausting your wings in vain? A great fire has broken out, burning the forest and the wilderness; how could your tiny body possibly extinguish it?" The pheasant replied, "Who is it that speaks?" He said, "I am the Heavenly Emperor Śakra." The pheasant said, "Today, the Heavenly Emperor possesses great merit and power, and there is no desire he cannot fulfill; to relieve disasters and rescue those in distress should be as easy as pointing to one's own palm. Yet you instead question my lack of success—where does the blame truly lie? The fierce fire is currently raging; do not speak further!" It then flew off again to head toward the flowing water. The Heavenly Emperor then scooped up water with his hands and sprinkled it over the forest; the fire was extinguished and the smoke vanished, the lives of all creatures were saved, and thus it is now called the Fire-extinguishing Stūpa (救火窣堵波).  Not far from the side of the place where the pheasant extinguished the fire, there is a stūpa marking the place where the Tathāgata, while practicing the Bodhisattva path, saved lives as a deer. In the remote past, there was a great forest here; a fire broke out in the wilderness, and the birds and beasts were driven to desperation, facing the peril of a swift current in front and the hardship of a raging fire behind, such that none escaped drowning or losing their lives. The deer, moved by compassion, positioned its body across the current, its skin pierced and bones broken, forcing itself to rescue the drowning. A lame hare arrived last, and the deer, enduring its fatigue and pain, rescued it as well. When its strength was exhausted, it drowned and died. The devas gathered its remains and erected a stūpa. Not far to the west of where the deer rescued the drowning, there is a stūpa. This is the place where Subhadra (蘇跋陀羅) (in the Tang language, "Good and Virtuous" [善賢]; formerly called Xubatuoluo [須跋陀羅], which is incorrect) entered into extinction. This Good and Virtuous one was originally a Brahmin teacher. He was one hundred and twenty years old, an elder of great wisdom. Hearing that the Buddha was about to enter extinction, he arrived at the twin trees and asked Ānanda, "The Buddha, the World-honored One, is about to enter extinction. I have doubts and hesitations, and I wish to ask him questions." Ānanda said, "The Buddha is about to enter nirvāṇa; please do not disturb him." He replied, "I have heard that it is difficult to encounter a Buddha in the world and difficult to hear the true Dharma. I have deep doubts and fear that I will have no one to ask." Subhadra then entered and first asked the Buddha, "Are there various other groups who call themselves teachers, each having different doctrines, handing down instructions to guide the laity—can Gautama (formerly called Qutan [瞿曇], which is a corruption and abbreviation) know them all?" The Buddha said, "I have thoroughly investigated them all," and then he expounded them for him. Having heard this, Subhadra’s mind was purified and he gained faith and understanding. He requested to enter the Dharma and receive the full ordination. The Tathāgata said to him, "Are you able to do so? For those of other paths and different schools who wish to practice the holy life, they must be tested for four years. By observing their conduct and examining their nature—if their deportment is tranquil and their speech is truthful—then they may practice the holy life in my Dharma. It depends on the person's conduct; how could this be difficult?" Subhadra said, "The World-honored One is compassionate and merciful, bestowing salvation without partiality. If one is tested for four years, the three karmas will then be in accord." The Buddha said, "I have already said that it depends on the person's conduct!" Thereupon, Subhadra (善賢) renounced the household life, immediately received the full precepts, and diligently practiced with a courageous body and mind. Before long, he had no doubts regarding the Dharma and personally attained realization. Before the night was far advanced, he attained the fruit of an Arhat; all his outflows were exhausted, and his holy life was established. Unable to bear seeing the Buddha enter mahānirvāṇa, he entered the fire-element samādhi (火界定) amidst the assembly, manifested supernatural powers, and entered nirvana first. This was the Tathāgata's final disciple, who attained extinction first; he is the one who, in the past, was the hare that crossed the river last. Beside the spot where Subhadra entered nirvana, there is a stūpa; this is the place where the Vajra-holder (執金剛) fell to the ground.  The Greatly Compassionate World-honored One, having appeared to benefit beings according to their capacities, finished his work of transformation and entered the joy of extinction, lying down with his head to the north between the twin trees. When the Vajra-holding deity, the Guhyapāda Malla (密迹力士), saw the Buddha enter nirvana, he cried out in bitter grief: "The Tathāgata has forsaken me and entered mahānirvāṇa; I have no refuge and no protection; the poisoned arrow has struck deep, and the fire of sorrow burns fiercely!" He cast aside his vajra-club and fell to the ground in a swoon. After a long time, he rose again, filled with sorrow and longing, and they said to one another: "In the great ocean of birth and death, who will serve as the boat and oar? In the long night of ignorance, who will serve as the lamp and torch?" Beside the spot where the Vajra-holder fell to the ground, there is a stūpa; this is the place where the Tathāgata was venerated for seven days after his nirvana. When the Tathāgata was about to enter nirvana, a brilliant light shone everywhere. Humans and devas gathered in full, all feeling deep sorrow and emotion, saying to one another: "The Great Awakened World-Honored One is now about to enter nirvana; the merit of sentient beings is exhausted, and the world is left without a refuge." The Tathāgata lay on his right side on a lion-couch and addressed the great assembly: "Do not say that the Tathāgata has entered final nirvana. The Dharma-body is eternally abiding and free from all change. You should abandon sloth and seek liberation early." The bhikṣus sobbed and grieved. At that time, Aniruddha (阿泥𢫫陀) (𢫫 is read 盧骨反, i.e. *lu[t]*; formerly called Analü [阿那律], which is incorrect) told the bhikṣus: "Stop, stop! Do not grieve; the devas will mock and wonder at you." When the Malla people had finished their offerings and wished to lift the golden coffin to proceed to the cremation ground (涅疊般那), Aniruddha said: "Wait! The devas wish to keep it for seven days to make offerings." Thereupon, the host of devas held exquisite heavenly flowers, wandered through the void, praised the holy virtues, and each exhausted their sincere hearts to join in making offerings. Beside the place where the coffin rested, there is a stūpa; this is the spot where Lady Mahāmāyā wept for the Buddha. After the Tathāgata had entered nirvana and the encoffining was completed, Aniruddha ascended to the heavenly palace and informed Lady Mahāmāyā, saying: "The Great Holy Dharma King has now entered nirvana." Upon hearing this, Mahāmāyā was choked with grief and fainted. She went with the assembly of devas to the space between the twin trees, where she saw the saṃghāṭi (monastic robe), the pātra (alms bowl), and the khakkhara (pewter staff). Stroking them, she wailed in agony, fainting and then regaining her voice to cry out: "The merit of humans and devas is exhausted, and the Eye of the World is extinguished! Now these objects are empty and without a master." By the holy power of the Tathāgata, the golden coffin opened of its own accord, emitting a great light; he sat up with palms joined and consoled his compassionate mother: "You have descended from a great distance! All conditioned things are by nature such; I pray you, do not grieve so deeply." Ānanda, suppressing his sorrow, asked the Buddha: "If future generations ask me, how shall I answer them?" He replied: "Say that after the Buddha had entered nirvana, his compassionate mother Mahāmāyā descended from the heavenly palace to the space between the twin trees, and for the sake of unfilial sentient beings, the Tathāgata rose from his golden coffin and preached the Dharma with his palms joined."

zh: 城西北三四里，渡阿恃多伐底河（唐言無勝，此世共稱耳。舊云阿利羅跋提河，訛也。典言謂之尸賴拏伐底河，譯曰有金河）。
en_current: Three or four li to the northwest of the city, one crosses the Ajitavatī River (阿恃多伐底河) (translated into Chinese as "Invincible"; this is merely the name commonly used in the world. It was formerly called the Alirabati River, which is an error. In the classical language it is called the Hiraṇyavatī River, which translates as "River Possessing Gold").

zh: 城北渡河三百餘步，有窣堵波，是如來焚身之處。地今黃黑，土雜灰炭，至誠求請，或得舍利。如來寂滅，人、天悲感，七寶為棺，千㲲纏身，設香華，建幡蓋，末羅之眾奉輿發引，前後導從，北渡金河，盛滿香油，積多香木，縱火以焚，二㲲不燒，一極𭣋身，一最覆外。為諸眾生分散舍利，唯有髮、爪儼然無損。焚身側有窣堵波，如來為大迦葉波現雙足處。如來金棺已下，香木已積，火燒不然，眾咸驚駭。阿泥𢫫陀言：「待迦葉波耳。」時大迦葉波與五百弟子自山林來，至拘尸城，問阿難曰：「世尊之身，可得見耶？」阿難曰：「千㲲纏絡，重棺周斂，香木已積，即事焚燒。」是時佛於棺內為出雙足，輪相之上，見有異色。問阿難曰：「何以有此？」曰：「佛初涅槃，人、天悲慟，眾淚迸染，致斯異色。」迦葉波作禮，旋繞興讚，香木自然，大火熾盛。故如來寂滅，三從棺出：初出臂，問阿難治路；次起坐，為母說法；後現雙足，示大迦葉波。現足側有窣堵波，無憂王所建也，是八王分舍利處。前建石柱，刻記其事。佛入涅槃，後涅疊般那已，諸八國王備四兵至，遣直性婆羅門謂拘尸力士曰：「天、人導師，此國寂滅，故自遠來，請分舍利。」力士曰：「如來降尊，即斯下土，滅世間明導，喪眾生慈父。如來舍利，自當供養，徒疲道路，終無得獲。」時諸大王遜辭以求，既不相允，重謂之曰：「禮請不從，兵威非遠。」直性婆羅門揚言曰：「念哉！大悲世尊忍修福善，彌歷曠劫，想所具聞，今欲相凌，此非宜也。今舍利在此，當均八分，各得供養，何至興兵？」諸力士依其言，即時均量，欲作八分。帝釋謂諸王曰：「天當有分，勿恃力競。」阿那婆答多龍王、文隣龍王、醫那鉢呾羅龍王復作是議：「無遺我曹。若以力者，眾非敵矣。」直性婆羅門曰：「勿諠諍也，宜共分之。」即作三分，一諸天，二龍眾，三留人間，八國重分。天、龍、人王，莫不悲感。
en_current: Crossing the river more than three hundred paces to the north of the city, there is a stupa, which is the place where the Tathāgata (如來) was cremated. The ground is now yellow and black, the soil mixed with ash and charcoal; if one requests with utmost sincerity, one may obtain relics. When the Tathāgata entered into extinction, humans and devas were moved by grief; they made a coffin of the seven treasures and wrapped his body in a thousand layers of fine cotton, offered incense and flowers, and set up banners and canopies. The Malla (末羅) people then bore the hearse in a procession, with guides in front and followers behind, crossing the Gold River to the north, where they filled it with fragrant oil, piled up much scented wood, and set it ablaze. Two layers of the cotton did not burn: one that was closest to the body and one that covered the outermost layer. In order to distribute the relics for all sentient beings, only the hair and nails remained intact and undamaged. Beside the place of cremation is a stupa, marking the spot where the Tathāgata revealed his two feet to Mahākāśyapa (大迦葉波). When the Tathāgata’s golden coffin had been lowered and the fragrant wood piled up, the fire would not ignite, and the assembly was filled with alarm. Aniruddha (阿泥𢫫陀) said, "We must wait for Kāśyapa." At that time, Mahākāśyapa, with five hundred disciples, came from the mountain forests and arrived at the city of Kuśinagara (拘尸城). He asked Ānanda, "Can the body of the World-Honored One still be seen?" Ānanda replied, "It is wrapped in a thousand layers of fine cotton, enclosed in heavy coffins, and the fragrant wood has already been piled up; the cremation is about to take place." At that moment, the Buddha, from within the coffin, revealed his two feet; upon the wheel-marks, a strange color was visible. He asked Ānanda, "Why is there this color?" He replied, "When the Buddha first entered parinirvāṇa, humans and devas were overcome with grief, and the tears of the multitude splashed and stained it, causing this strange color." Kāśyapa paid homage, circumambulated, and offered praises; the fragrant wood ignited spontaneously, and a great fire blazed fiercely. Thus, when the Tathāgata entered extinction, he emerged from the coffin three times: first, he extended his arm to ask Ānanda about the path; next, he sat up to preach the Dharma for his mother; finally, he revealed his two feet to show them to Mahākāśyapa. Beside the place where he revealed his feet is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王), which is the site where the eight kings divided the relics. In front of it, a stone pillar was erected, inscribed with an account of the event. After the Buddha had entered nirvāṇa and the cremation was completed, the kings of eight countries arrived with their fourfold armies and dispatched a straightforward Brahmin to say to the Mallas of Kuśinagara (拘尸力士), "The Teacher of gods and men has entered extinction in this country; therefore, we have come from afar to request a share of the relics." The Mallas replied, "The Tathāgata descended in his majesty to this lower realm; here the bright guide of the world has been extinguished and we have lost the compassionate father of all living beings. The relics of the Tathāgata should naturally be worshipped by us alone; you have wearied yourselves on the road in vain, for you shall never obtain them." At that time, the various great kings requested them with humble words, but since they were not granted, they said again, "If polite requests are not followed, the might of our armies is not far off." The straightforward Brahmin spoke aloud, "Reflect! The Greatly Compassionate World-Honored One patiently cultivated merit and goodness throughout vast kalpas, as I presume you have all heard; it is not appropriate for you now to seek to oppress one another. Since the relics are here, they should be divided into eight equal portions so that each may receive them for worship; why go so far as to raise troops?" The Mallas followed his words and immediately measured the relics, intending to divide them into eight portions. Śakra (帝釋) said to the kings, "The heavens should have a share; do not rely on force to compete." The Nāga kings Anavatapta (阿那婆答多), Mucilinda (文隣), and Elāpattra (醫那鉢呾羅) also proposed, "Do not exclude us. If it comes to force, the masses are no match for us." The straightforward Brahmin said, "Do not clamor and contend; it is proper to divide them together." He immediately made three portions: first for the devas, second for the Nāga host, and third to remain among humans, which the eight kingdoms then subdivided. The devas, Nāgas, and human kings were all moved to sorrow.

zh: 分舍利窣堵波西南行二百餘里，至大邑聚。有婆羅門，豪右巨富，確乎不雜，學究五明，敬崇三寶。接其居側，建立僧坊，窮諸資用，備盡珍飾，或有眾僧往來中路，慇懃請留，罄心供養，或止一宿，乃至七日。其後設賞迦王毀壞佛法，眾僧絕侶，歲月驟淹，而婆羅門每懷懇惻。經行之次，見一沙門，厖眉皓髮，杖錫而來。婆羅門馳往迎逆，問所從至，請入僧坊，備諸供養，旦以淳乳，煮粥進焉。沙門受已，纔一嚌齒，便即置鉢，沈吟長息。婆羅門持食，跪而問曰：「大德慧利隨緣，幸見臨顧，為夕不安耶？為粥不味乎？」沙門愍然告曰：「吾悲眾生福祐漸薄，斯言且置，食已方說。」沙門食訖，攝衣即語。婆羅門曰：「向許有說，今何無言？」沙門告曰：「吾非忘也。談不容易，事或致疑。必欲得聞，今當略說。吾向所歎，非薄汝粥。自數百年，不嘗此味。昔如來在世，我時預從，在王舍城竹林精舍，俯清流而滌器，或以澡漱，或以盥沐。嗟乎！今之淳乳，不及古之淡水，此乃人、天福滅使之然也。」婆羅門曰：「然則大德乃親見佛耶？」沙門曰：「然。汝豈不聞佛子羅怙羅者，我身是也。為護正法，未入寂滅。」說是語已，忽然不見。婆羅門遂以所宿之房，塗香灑掃，像設儀肅，其敬如在。復大林中行五百餘里，至婆羅痆（女黠反）斯國（舊曰波羅柰國，訛也。中印度境）。
en_current: Traveling two hundred-odd *li* southwest from the relic stūpa, one arrives at a large town (大邑聚). There was a brāhmaṇa there, a man of great wealth and high standing, whose lineage was pure and unmixed, who had mastered the five sciences (pañcavidyā), and who deeply revered the Three Jewels. Adjacent to his residence, he established a monastery, exhausting his resources to provide it with every adornment. Whenever members of the saṅgha traveled along that road, he would earnestly invite them to stay, offering them his wholehearted support, whether they stopped for a single night or for as long as seven days. Later, when King Śaśāṅka (設賞迦王) destroyed the Buddha-dharma, the saṅgha was dispersed and the years passed quickly, yet the brāhmaṇa remained filled with sincere sorrow. While walking in meditation, he saw a śramaṇa with bushy eyebrows and white hair approaching, leaning on a staff. The brāhmaṇa hurried to welcome him, asked where he had come from, and invited him into the monastery, where he prepared every kind of offering, including a morning meal of porridge cooked with pure milk. The śramaṇa accepted it, but after tasting only a morsel, he set down his bowl and sighed deeply. The brāhmaṇa, holding the food, knelt and asked, "Great Virtuous One, whose wisdom and merit follow conditions, I am fortunate to have your presence; were you uncomfortable during the night, or was the porridge not to your taste?" The śramaṇa replied with compassion, "I grieve that the merit and blessings of sentient beings are gradually thinning. Let that matter rest for now; I will speak after I have eaten." Once the śramaṇa had finished eating, he adjusted his robes and spoke. The brāhmaṇa said, "You previously promised to speak; why are you silent now?" The śramaṇa replied, "I have not forgotten. What I have to discuss is not easy, and the matter may invite doubt. If you truly wish to hear it, I shall now speak of it briefly." "What I sighed about just now was not to disparage your porridge. For several hundred years, I have not tasted such a flavor. Long ago, when the Tathāgata was in the world, I was in his retinue at the Bamboo Grove Monastery (Veṇuvana-vihāra) in the city of Rājagṛha, where I would lean over the clear stream to wash the vessels, or use the water for rinsing and bathing. Alas! The rich milk of today cannot compare to the plain water of old; this is because the merit of humans and devas has been exhausted." The brāhmaṇa asked, "In that case, does the Venerable One mean that you personally saw the Buddha?" The śramaṇa replied, "Indeed. Have you not heard of the Buddha’s son, Rāhula? I am he. To protect the True Dharma, I have not yet entered final extinction." Having said these words, he suddenly vanished. The brāhmaṇa then anointed and swept the room where he had stayed, set up an image with solemn ceremony, and paid his respects as if he were still present. Traveling further through the great forest for more than five hundred li, one arrives at the country of Vārāṇasī (婆羅痆斯國) (痆 is read 女黠反; formerly called Poluonai, which is incorrect. It is in the region of Central India).

zh: 雉救火側不遠，有窣堵波，是如來修菩薩行時，為鹿救生之處。乃往古昔，此有大林，火炎中野，飛走窮窘，前有駛流之阨，後困猛火之難，莫不沈溺，喪棄身命。其鹿惻隱，身據橫流，穿皮斷骨，自強拯溺。蹇兔後至，忍疲苦而濟之。筋力既竭，溺水而死。諸天收骸，起窣堵波。
en_current: Not far from the side of the place where the pheasant saved the fire, there is a stūpa; this is the place where the Tathāgata, while practicing the bodhisattva path, saved lives as a deer. In the remote past, there was a great forest here. A fire broke out in the wilderness, and the flying and running creatures were driven to desperation; facing the peril of a swift current in front and the hardship of a raging fire behind, there were none who did not drown or lose their lives. The deer, moved by compassion, positioned its body across the current, its skin torn and bones broken, exerting itself to rescue the drowning. A lame hare arrived later, and the deer, enduring fatigue and suffering, helped it across. Once its strength was exhausted, it drowned and died. The various devas gathered its remains and erected a stūpa.

zh: 鹿拯溺西不遠，有窣堵波，是蘇跋陀羅（唐言善賢。舊曰須跋陀羅，訛也）入寂滅之處。善賢者，本梵志師也。年百二十，耆舊多智。聞佛寂滅，至雙樹間，問阿難曰：「佛世尊將寂滅，我懷疑滯，願欲請問。」阿難曰：「佛將涅槃，幸無擾也。」曰：「吾聞佛世難遇，正法難聞，我有深疑，恐無所請。」善賢遂入，先問佛言：「有諸別眾，自稱為師，各有異法，垂訓導俗，喬答摩（舊曰瞿曇，訛略也）能盡知耶？」佛言：「吾悉深究。」乃為演說。善賢聞已，心淨信解，求入法中，受具足戒。如來告曰：「汝豈能耶？外道異學修梵行者，當試四歲，觀其行，察其性，威儀寂靜，辭語誠實，則可於我法中淨修梵行。在人行耳，斯何難哉！」善賢曰：「世尊悲愍，含濟無私，四歲試學，三業方順。」佛言：「我先已說，在人行耳！」於是善賢出家，即受具戒，勤勵修習，身心勇猛。已而於法無疑，自身作證。夜分未久，果證羅漢，諸漏已盡，梵行已立。不忍見佛入大涅槃，即於眾中入火界定，現神通事，而先寂滅。是為如來最後弟子，乃先滅度，即昔後渡蹇兔是也。
en_current: Not far to the west of the place where the deer was rescued from drowning, there is a stūpa. This is the place where Subhadra (蘇跋陀羅; in Chinese, Good and Virtuous; the old form Xubatuoluo 須跋陀羅 is erroneous) entered into extinction. This Good and Virtuous one was originally a master of the Brahmins. He was one hundred and twenty years old, an elder of great wisdom. Hearing that the Buddha was about to enter extinction, he went to the twin trees and asked Ānanda, "The Buddha, the World-honored One, is about to enter extinction. I have doubts and hesitations, and I wish to ask him questions." Ānanda said, "The Buddha is about to enter nirvāṇa; please do not disturb him." He replied, "I have heard that it is difficult to encounter a Buddha in the world and difficult to hear the true Dharma. I have deep doubts and fear that I will have no one to ask." Good and Virtuous then entered and first asked the Buddha, "There are various other groups who call themselves teachers, each having different doctrines, handing down instructions to guide the laity. Can Gautama (喬答摩; the old form Qutan 瞿曇 is erroneous and abbreviated) know them all?" The Buddha said, "I have thoroughly investigated them all," and then he expounded them for him. Having heard this, Good and Virtuous had a purified mind and clear understanding; he sought to enter the Dharma and receive the full ordination. The Tathāgata said to him, "Are you truly able to do so? For those of other paths and different schools who wish to practice the holy life, they must be tested for four years. By observing their conduct and examining their nature, if their deportment is tranquil and their speech is truthful, then they may practice the holy life in my Dharma. It depends on the person's conduct; how could this be difficult!" Good and Virtuous said, "The World-honored One is compassionate and merciful, saving and benefiting without partiality. As for the four-year probationary study, my three actions will be in accordance." The Buddha said, "As I have said before, it simply depends on a person's own practice!" Thereupon Subhadra (善賢) left the home-life and received full ordination, diligently applying himself to cultivation with a courageous body and mind. Soon he had no doubts regarding the Dharma and personally attained realization. Before the night was far spent, he attained the fruit of an arhat; his outflows were exhausted and the holy life was established. Unable to bear seeing the Buddha enter the great mahāparinirvāṇa, he entered the samādhi of the fire element (tejo-dhātu-samādhi) amidst the assembly, manifested supernatural powers, and entered extinction first. He was the Tathāgata’s last disciple, yet he entered extinction first; he was the lame hare (蹇兔) who was the last to be ferried across in a former life.

en_current: Beside the spot where he showed his feet is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王), which is the place where the eight kings divided the relics. In front of it stands a stone pillar, on which this event is inscribed. After the Buddha entered nirvāṇa and the cremation was completed, the kings of eight countries arrived with their fourfold armies and dispatched the honest Brahmin to say to the Mallas of Kuśinagara (拘尸力士), "The Teacher of gods and men has entered extinction in this country; therefore, we have come from afar to request a share of the relics." The Mallas replied, "The Tathāgata descended in his majesty to this lower world; now that the light of the world has been extinguished and the compassionate father of all living beings is lost, the Tathāgata’s relics should naturally be worshipped by us alone. You have wearied yourselves on the road in vain; you will ultimately obtain nothing." At that time, the great kings requested them with humble words, but since they were not granted their request, they said again, "If polite requests are not followed, the might of our armies is not far off." The honest Brahmin then spoke out loudly, "Reflect! The Greatly Compassionate World-Honored One has practiced patience and accumulated merit over vast eons, as you have surely heard. To now wish to bully one another is not appropriate. Since the relics are here, they should be divided into eight equal portions so that each may receive them for worship; why go so far as to raise troops?" The Mallas followed his words and immediately measured the relics, intending to divide them into eight portions. Śakra (帝釋) said to the kings, "The gods should also have a share; do not rely on force to compete." The Anavatapta (阿那婆答多) Dragon King, the Mucilinda (文隣) Dragon King, and the Elāpatra (醫那鉢呾羅) Dragon King also made this proposal: "Do not leave us out. If it is a matter of force, the masses are no match for us." The honest-natured Brahmin (直性婆羅門) said, "Do not quarrel; it is proper to divide them together." He immediately made three portions: first for the heavenly beings, second for the assembly of dragons, and third to remain in the human world, where the eight nations further divided them. The heavenly beings, the dragons, and the human kings were all moved with grief and gratitude.

zh: 婆羅痆斯國，周四千餘里。國大都城西臨殑伽河，長十八九里，廣五六里。閭閻櫛比，居人殷盛，家積巨萬，室盈奇貨。人性溫恭，俗重強學，多信外道，少敬佛法。氣序和，穀稼盛，果木扶疎，茂草靃靡。伽藍三十餘所，僧徒三千餘人，並學小乘正量部法。天祠百餘所，外道萬餘人，並多宗事大自在天，或斷髮，或椎髻，露形無服，塗身以灰，精勤苦行，求出生死。大城中天祠二十所，層臺祠宇，雕石文木，茂林相蔭，清流交帶，鍮石天像量減百尺，威嚴肅然，懍懍如在。
en_current: The country of Vārāṇasī (婆羅痆斯國) is over four thousand li in circumference. The capital city of the country borders the Gaṅgā (殑伽河) River to the west; it is eighteen or nineteen li long and five or six li wide. The houses are arranged like the teeth of a comb, the inhabitants are prosperous, families possess vast wealth, and their rooms are filled with rare goods. The people are gentle and respectful by nature, and the customs value diligent study; many believe in non-Buddhist paths, and few respect the Buddha-dharma. The climate is temperate, cereal crops are abundant, fruit trees grow luxuriantly, and the grasses are lush and thick. There are more than thirty saṃghārāmas with over three thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Sammatiya school (正量部) of the Lesser Vehicle. There are over one hundred deva temples with more than ten thousand followers of other paths, most of whom worship Maheśvara; some cut their hair, others wear it in a topknot, they go naked without clothing and smear their bodies with ash, diligently practicing austerities to seek liberation from birth and death. Within the great city are twenty deva temples with multi-storied terraces and shrines made of carved stone and ornamented wood, shaded by luxuriant forests and encircled by clear streams; there is a brass statue of the deity nearly one hundred feet tall, solemn and majestic as if it were alive.

name_zh: 婆羅痆河西無憂王窣堵波・石柱
zh: 大城東北婆羅痆河西有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也，高百餘尺。前建石柱，碧鮮若鏡，光潤凝流，其中常現如來影像。
